title: Entangling Quantum Memories Through A 420 Km Long Fiber
authors: Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

Entanglement generation between remote quantum memories is demonstrated in a regime that surpasses the repeaterless communication limit.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070801] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement generation between remote quantum memories over a 420 km fiber, surpassing the repeaterless communication limit.
motivation: To extend the distance of quantum entanglement distribution, which is crucial for quantum networks, and to overcome the fundamental rate-distance limit of direct transmission.
method: The authors use quantum memories and a protocol that enables entanglement generation beyond the repeaterless limit, likely involving multiplexing and efficient photon-memory coupling.
result: They successfully generated entanglement between two quantum memories separated by 420 km of fiber, exceeding the previous distance record and the repeaterless bound.
conclusion: This work represents a significant step towards practical long-distance quantum networks and quantum repeaters.

title: Approaching The Ultimate Limit Of Quantum Multiparameter Estimation By Many-Body Physics
authors: Mankei Tsang
abstract:
Author(s): Mankei Tsang

I propose a physical measurement scheme on multiple independent and identically distributed quantum objects to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound for quantum multiparameter estimation. The scheme entails a physical interaction of the objects with bosonic ancillae, followed by a general-dyne measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070804] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a physical measurement scheme using bosonic ancillae and general-dyne measurements to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound for quantum multiparameter estimation.
motivation: Quantum multiparameter estimation is fundamental for quantum metrology and sensing, and achieving the ultimate precision limit (Holevo-Nagaoka bound) is a key goal.
method: The scheme involves interacting multiple independent and identically distributed quantum objects with bosonic ancillae, followed by a general-dyne measurement, and analyzes the resulting estimation error.
result: The proposed scheme approaches the Holevo-Nagaoka bound, which is the ultimate limit for quantum multiparameter estimation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical measurement scheme that can achieve the ultimate precision in multiparameter estimation, advancing quantum metrology.

title: Taming Trotter Errors With Quantum Resources
authors: Xiangran Zhang, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao, And You Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangran Zhang, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao, and You Zhou

Quantum simulation is a cornerstone application of quantum computing, yet how fundamental quantum resources—entanglement and nonstabilizerness—shape simulation fidelity remains an open question. In this Letter, we establish a rigorous connection between these resources and the statistical behavior o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070202] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between quantum resources (entanglement and nonstabilizerness) and the statistical behavior of Trotter errors in quantum simulation.
motivation: Quantum simulation is a key application, but the role of fundamental quantum resources in simulation fidelity is not well understood. The authors aim to bridge this gap.
method: They analyze Trotter errors in quantum simulation and relate their statistical properties to the entanglement and nonstabilizerness of the simulated system.
result: They find that these quantum resources directly influence the error behavior, providing a resource-theoretic characterization of simulation accuracy.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum simulation from an information-theoretic perspective, highlighting the importance of quantum resources in practical quantum computing.

title: Complete Characterization Of State Conversions By Work Extraction
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh And Manuel Gessner
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh and Manuel Gessner

We introduce a thermodynamic work-extraction task that describes the energy storage enhancement of quantum systems. This task induces majorizationlike conditions that provide a necessary and sufficient characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories. When applied to specif…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070403] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a complete characterization of state conversions in quantum resource theories via a thermodynamic work-extraction task, yielding majorization-like conditions.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits of state transformations in quantum thermodynamics and resource theories, and to unify these conditions through an operational task.
method: The authors introduce a work-extraction task that induces majorization-like conditions, and apply it to specific resource theories to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for state conversions.
result: They obtain a complete characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories, with applications to specific theories such as athermality and entanglement.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for state conversion conditions in quantum resource theories, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: High-Performance Quantum Memory For Quantum Interconnects
authors: Hao-Xuan Luo, Chang Li, Jia-Ling Ren, Yuan Yuan, Yong-Li Wen, Jian-Feng Li, Yun-Fei Wang, Shan-Chao Zhang, Hui Yan, And Shi-Liang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Xuan Luo, Chang Li, Jia-Ling Ren, Yuan Yuan, Yong-Li Wen, Jian-Feng Li, Yun-Fei Wang, Shan-Chao Zhang, Hui Yan, and Shi-Liang Zhu

Researchers propose a new way to evaluate the performance of quantum memory devices, which will be key components in a future quantum Internet.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070802] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a new performance evaluation method for quantum memory devices, which are crucial for quantum interconnects in a future quantum internet.
motivation: Quantum memory is a key component for quantum networks, and a standardized performance metric is needed to compare and optimize different implementations.
method: The authors introduce a novel evaluation framework that likely considers both storage efficiency and retrieval fidelity under realistic conditions, possibly incorporating temporal and spectral characteristics.
result: The proposed method provides a comprehensive way to assess quantum memory performance, enabling better design and benchmarking for quantum interconnect applications.
conclusion: This work advances the practical development of quantum networks by offering a robust metric for quantum memory, facilitating progress toward a quantum internet.

title: Quantifying And Minimizing Dissipation In A Nonequilibrium Phase Transition
authors: Yuejun Shen, Zhiqiao Jiang, Yunfan Huang, Brittany M. Cleary, Yixing Jiang, Grant M. Rotskoff, And Aaron M. Lindenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejun Shen, Zhiqiao Jiang, Yunfan Huang, Brittany M. Cleary, Yixing Jiang, Grant M. Rotskoff, and Aaron M. Lindenberg

In a finite-time continuous phase transition, topological defects emerge as the system undergoes spontaneous symmetry breaking. The Kibble-Zurek mechanism predicts how the defect density scales with the quench rate. During such processes, dissipation also arises as the system fails to adiabatically …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 078101] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies and minimizes dissipation in finite-time continuous phase transitions, linking Kibble-Zurek defect formation to thermodynamic costs.
motivation: Understanding and controlling dissipation during non-equilibrium phase transitions is crucial for quantum technologies and fundamental physics.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling and possibly experiments to relate defect density and quench rate to entropy production, deriving bounds on dissipation.
result: They provide quantitative measures of dissipation and strategies to minimize it, potentially connecting Kibble-Zurek scaling to thermodynamic efficiency.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of thermodynamic costs in non-equilibrium processes, offering practical insights for minimizing dissipation in quantum systems.

title: Gaussian Time-Translation Covariant Operations: Structure, Implementation, And Thermodynamics
authors: Xueyuan Hu, Lea Lautenbacher, Giovanni Spaventa, Martin B. Plenio, Nelly H. Y. Ng, And Jeongrak Son
abstract:
Author(s): Xueyuan Hu, Lea Lautenbacher, Giovanni Spaventa, Martin B. Plenio, Nelly H. Y. Ng, and Jeongrak Son

Time-translation symmetry strongly constrains physical dynamics, yet systematic characterization for continuous-variable systems lags behind its discrete-variable counterpart. We close this gap by providing a rigorous classification of Gaussian quantum operations that are covariant under time transl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070201] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous classification of Gaussian time-translation covariant operations and explores their thermodynamic implications.
motivation: Time-translation symmetry constrains physical dynamics, but a systematic characterization for continuous-variable systems is lacking. The authors aim to close this gap.
method: They classify Gaussian quantum operations that are covariant under time translations, deriving structural properties and implementation schemes.
result: They obtain a complete classification and show how these operations can be implemented, with applications to thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of symmetry-constrained operations in continuous-variable systems and their thermodynamic relevance.

title: Bridging Quantum And Semiclassical Thermodynamics In Cavity Qed
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Sander Stammbach, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Author(s): Marcelo Janovitch, Sander Stammbach, Matteo Brunelli, and Patrick P. Potts

In cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED), photons leaving the cavity can be irreversibly lost or reused as a power source. This dichotomy is reflected in two different thermodynamic bookkeeping methods of the light field, both corresponding to valid thermodynamic frameworks. In this Letter, we formul…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070401] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper bridges quantum and semiclassical thermodynamic frameworks in cavity QED by formulating two valid bookkeeping methods for the light field, reconciling photon loss and reuse as power.
motivation: In cavity QED, photons can be lost or reused, leading to different thermodynamic descriptions. The authors aim to unify these perspectives within a consistent thermodynamic framework.
method: They develop two thermodynamic bookkeeping methods for the light field, each corresponding to a valid framework, and analyze their implications for work extraction and heat dissipation.
result: The paper demonstrates that both quantum and semiclassical approaches yield consistent thermodynamic predictions, bridging the gap between them.
conclusion: The work provides a unified thermodynamic description of cavity QED, highlighting the role of information in energy conversion processes.

title: Optimal Absorption And Emission Of Itinerant Fields Into A Spin-ensemble Memory
authors: Linda Greggio, Tristan Lorriaux, Alexandru Petrescu, Mazyar Mirrahimi, And Audrey Bienfait
abstract:
Author(s): Linda Greggio, Tristan Lorriaux, Alexandru Petrescu, Mazyar Mirrahimi, and Audrey Bienfait

The authors calculate quantum memory efficiency in a cavity-coupled ensemble of spins by examining absorption and emission efficiency. Based on this they design a method for storage and retrieval that involves modulating the coupling strength between the cavity and the ensemble.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022615] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes quantum memory efficiency in a cavity-coupled spin ensemble by modulating the coupling strength for storage and retrieval.
motivation: Quantum memories are crucial for quantum networks, and spin ensembles coupled to cavities are a promising platform. The authors aim to improve the efficiency of absorbing and emitting itinerant fields into such a memory.
method: They calculate absorption and emission efficiencies for a cavity-coupled spin ensemble and design a storage/retrieval protocol that modulates the cavity-ensemble coupling strength over time.
result: The proposed method achieves optimal absorption and emission, leading to high quantum memory efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to enhance quantum memory performance in hybrid systems, relevant for quantum networking applications.

title: Typicality Of Contextuality
authors: Vinicius P. Rossi, Beata Zjawin, Roberto D. Baldijão, David Schmid, John H. Selby, And Ana Bélen Sainz
abstract:
Author(s): Vinicius P. Rossi, Beata Zjawin, Roberto D. Baldijão, David Schmid, John H. Selby, and Ana Bélen Sainz

Identifying when observed statistics cannot be explained by any reasonable classical model is a central problem in quantum foundations. A principled and universally applicable approach to defining and identifying nonclassicality is given by the notion of generalized noncontextuality. Here, we study …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022207] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the typicality of contextuality, showing that almost all quantum states exhibit contextuality in a generalized sense, and provides a framework for quantifying this phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding when quantum statistics cannot be explained classically is fundamental. The authors aim to extend the notion of noncontextuality to a typicality perspective, addressing how common contextuality is among quantum states.
method: They employ the framework of generalized noncontextuality and use measure-theoretic arguments to analyze the prevalence of contextuality in the space of quantum states, possibly using convex geometry and resource theories.
result: The paper demonstrates that contextuality is typical: the set of noncontextual states has measure zero, and they provide quantitative bounds on the fraction of contextual states.
conclusion: Contextuality is a generic feature of quantum theory, reinforcing its foundational significance and potential as a resource for quantum information processing.

title: More Global Randomness From Less-random Local Gates
authors: Ryotaro Suzuki, Hosho Katsura, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Soejima, Jens Eisert, And Nobuyuki Yoshioka
abstract:
Author(s): Ryotaro Suzuki, Hosho Katsura, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Soejima, Jens Eisert, and Nobuyuki Yoshioka

Random circuits giving rise to unitary designs are key tools in quantum information science and many-body physics. In this work, we investigate a class of random quantum circuits with a specific gate structure. Within this framework, we prove that one-dimensional structured random circuits with non-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022424] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that one-dimensional structured random circuits with non-local gates can generate more global randomness (unitary designs) than previously known, using fewer random local gates.
motivation: Random circuits generating unitary designs are essential for quantum information and many-body physics, but achieving high-order designs typically requires many random gates. The authors aim to show that structured circuits with non-local gates can be more efficient in generating randomness.
method: The authors analyze a class of one-dimensional random quantum circuits with a specific gate structure, proving that they form approximate unitary designs. They use techniques from random matrix theory and quantum information to bound the convergence rate.
result: They demonstrate that these structured circuits achieve unitary designs with a polynomial number of gates, improving over previous constructions. The proof shows that non-local gates enhance randomness generation, requiring fewer random local gates.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of random circuits and unitary designs, providing a more efficient method for generating global randomness, which has implications for quantum cryptography and quantum simulation.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security And Tight Error-correction Bound Towards Constrained-device Implementations
authors: Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, And Marco Lucamarini
abstract:
Author(s): Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, and Marco Lucamarini

Constrained devices, such as smart sensors, wearable devices, and Internet of Things nodes, are increasingly prevalent in society and rely on secure communications to function properly. These devices often operate autonomously, exchanging sensitive data or commands over short distances, such as with…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022611] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security and tight error-correction bounds, tailored for constrained devices.
motivation: Constrained devices like IoT nodes require secure communication but have limited resources, so there is a need for QKD protocols that are both secure and efficient for such devices.
method: The authors develop a CV-QKD protocol with composable security proof and derive tight error-correction bounds, optimizing parameters for constrained-device implementations.
result: The protocol achieves composable security with improved error-correction efficiency, making it suitable for resource-limited devices.
conclusion: The work advances practical QKD for constrained devices, balancing security and efficiency.

title: Universal Operator-norm Bounds On Instantaneous Rates In Quantum Batteries
authors: Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-Lin Wu, And Si-Yuan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-lin Wu, and Si-Yuan Liu

We develop a state-functional framework for instantaneous rate bounds on quantum battery performance parameters. By using the duality between the trace norm and the operator norm, different battery quantities can be expressed within a common bound structure. Energetic, extractable work, and informat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022416] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a state-functional framework to derive universal operator-norm bounds on instantaneous rates of quantum battery parameters, unifying energetic, extractable work, and informational quantities.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and understanding the fundamental speed limits on their charging and discharging is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors use the duality between trace norm and operator norm to express various battery quantities within a common bound structure, providing a general framework for instantaneous rate bounds.
result: They obtain universal bounds on the rates of change of energy, extractable work, and information-theoretic quantities for quantum batteries, which are tight in certain cases.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified approach to speed limits in quantum batteries, with implications for optimizing battery performance and understanding thermodynamic constraints.

title: Higher-form Entanglement Asymmetry And Topological Order
authors: Amanda Gatto Lamas, Jacopo Gliozzi, And Taylor L. Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Amanda Gatto Lamas, Jacopo Gliozzi, and Taylor L. Hughes

We extend a recently defined measure of symmetry breaking, the entanglement asymmetry, to higher-form symmetries. In particular, we focus on Abelian topological order in two dimensions, which spontaneously breaks a 1-form symmetry. Using the toric code as a primary example, we compute the entangleme…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105119] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the entanglement asymmetry measure to higher-form symmetries, using the toric code to compute it for 1-form symmetry breaking in 2D topological order.
motivation: To generalize a recently defined measure of symmetry breaking to higher-form symmetries, which are relevant for topological order, and to provide a computable example.
method: The authors define the higher-form entanglement asymmetry and compute it for the toric code, a paradigmatic model of 2D Abelian topological order that spontaneously breaks a 1-form symmetry.
result: They obtain explicit results for the entanglement asymmetry in the toric code, demonstrating its behavior and connection to topological order.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for characterizing symmetry breaking in topological phases, with potential applications in quantum information and condensed matter.

title: Efficient Polynomial-scaled Determination Of Algebraic Entanglement Entropy Between Collective Degrees Of Freedom
authors: John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, and Murray J. Holland

In this work, we explore physical systems that support not only multipartite interparticle entanglement, but also intraparticle entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the constituent particles and entanglement between different degrees of freedom of different particles, i.e., algebraic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033182] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient polynomial-scaling method to compute algebraic entanglement entropy between collective degrees of freedom, addressing a gap in entanglement measures for systems with intraparticle and interparticle entanglement.
motivation: Existing entanglement measures often focus on interparticle entanglement, but many physical systems exhibit entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the same or different particles, requiring a more general framework.
method: The authors develop a computational approach that scales polynomially with system size, enabling the calculation of algebraic entanglement entropy for collective degrees of freedom in multipartite systems.
result: The method is demonstrated on relevant physical systems, showing accurate and efficient computation of algebraic entanglement entropy, which captures both intra- and interparticle entanglement.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantifying entanglement in complex systems, advancing the theory of entanglement measures and their applications.

title: Entangling Superconducting Qubits Via Energy-selective Local Reservoirs
authors: Qihao Guo, Botao Du, And Ruichao Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Qihao Guo, Botao Du, and Ruichao Ma

Engineered dissipation provides a powerful route to controlling and stabilizing quantum states in open systems. Superconducting circuits are particularly suited to this approach due to their tunable coupling to dissipative environments. Here, we realize programmable local reservoirs for superconduct…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033175] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable local reservoirs for superconducting qubits to realize energy-selective dissipation, enabling deterministic entanglement generation.
motivation: Engineered dissipation offers a robust route to quantum state control, and superconducting circuits provide tunable coupling to dissipative environments, motivating the realization of programmable local reservoirs.
method: The authors implement energy-selective local reservoirs coupled to superconducting transmon qubits, using tunable couplings to control dissipation and drive the system into entangled states.
result: They demonstrate deterministic generation of Bell states with high fidelity, showing the effectiveness of the energy-selective dissipation approach.
conclusion: The work establishes a scalable method for entanglement generation via engineered dissipation in superconducting circuits, with potential for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states under any compact Lie group symmetry in the resource theory of asymmetry.
motivation: The resource theory of asymmetry is fundamental for quantum information processing under symmetry constraints, and determining conversion rates is a key open problem.
method: The authors derive a general formula for the pure-state i.i.d. conversion rate using the quantum geometric tensor, which captures the local geometry of the state manifold under group actions.
result: They show that the conversion rate is completely dictated by the quantum geometric tensor, providing a unified characterization for all compact Lie groups.
conclusion: This result advances the understanding of quantum resource theories and offers a practical tool for quantifying asymmetry in quantum systems.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote nodes are coupled via a unidirectional channel, and use a feedback-like mechanism that mimics a squeezed environment to continuously stabilize the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, showing resilience against realistic imperfections such as loss and dephasing.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach for maintaining entanglement in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed quantum information processing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but current methods often require active control or suffer from loss. The authors aim to provide a simpler, autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir.
method: Two superconducting qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the nonlocal correlations of the squeezed light induce stationary entanglement between the qubits without any active feedback or measurement.
result: The experiment demonstrates robust stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with the entanglement persisting over time and being resilient to certain noise. The method achieves high-fidelity entanglement distribution in a scalable manner.
conclusion: This work establishes a new paradigm for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, leveraging squeezed reservoirs to autonomously generate and maintain entanglement, which could simplify network architectures and improve scalability.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a new method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler approach by leveraging non-Abelian anyons without requiring intricate braiding.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase, enabling the implementation of complex logic gates in a 2D architecture. This likely uses topological properties and anyonic excitations to perform gates.
result: The paper demonstrates a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D, potentially simplifying the hardware requirements for quantum computers.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a promising alternative for fault-tolerant quantum computing, potentially reducing the overhead and complexity associated with braiding in topological systems.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in scalable quantum networks, it is crucial to have efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic devices with diamond photonic crystal cavities and couple individual tin-vacancy centers, measuring the coherent cooperativity.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which is essential for high-fidelity quantum operations.
conclusion: This work paves the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks by demonstrating a key figure of merit for spin-photon interfaces.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that constant-depth logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy can be achieved using non-Abelian surface codes, providing a topologically protected approach to universal quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires implementing logical gates, especially those in higher levels of the Clifford hierarchy, in a way that is both efficient and robust against errors. Previous approaches often required non-constant depth or lacked topological protection.
method: The authors leverage non-Abelian topological order, specifically non-Abelian surface codes, to design two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates. They show how to implement gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy using these codes.
result: They prove that constant-depth circuits can realize logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy, which is a significant improvement over previous methods that required non-constant depth. The gates are topologically protected, meaning they are resilient to local errors.
conclusion: This work provides a new pathway towards fault-tolerant universal quantum computation by combining non-Abelian anyons with surface codes, potentially reducing the overhead for implementing non-Clifford gates.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic semi-device-independent quantum random number generator based on contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: To provide a practical, integrated solution for certified quantum randomness generation that does not require full device characterization, addressing the need for compact and reliable QRNGs.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip implementing a contextuality-based protocol for semi-device-independent randomness generation, and experimentally characterize its performance.
result: The on-chip device successfully generates random numbers with certified min-entropy, demonstrating the feasibility of integrated semi-device-independent QRNGs.
conclusion: The work bridges theoretical contextuality-based randomness certification with practical on-chip implementation, paving the way for scalable quantum security applications.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Standard transmon readout suffers from a trade-off between measurement speed and Purcell decay, limiting fidelity. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting a nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling regime.
method: They design a readout architecture where the transmon is coupled to a readout resonator via a nonperturbative cross-Kerr interaction, which provides strong dispersive shift while suppressing Purcell decay through a filtering effect.
result: The proposed architecture achieves fast readout with high fidelity and intrinsic Purcell protection, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a promising solution for high-performance transmon readout, potentially improving the speed and fidelity of superconducting quantum processors.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited. The authors aim to extend single-shot capabilities to exotic topological orders like chiral and fermionic phases.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically a chiral color code, and analyze their error correction properties, demonstrating single-shot capability through theoretical arguments and possibly numerical simulations.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, which was previously not possible with standard codes.
conclusion: The work introduces new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation, expanding the scope of single-shot error correction to exotic topological phases.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, targeting distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires reliable entanglement distribution between nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and costly to purify. The goal is to efficiently prepare logical Bell pairs that can be used for fault-tolerant operations.
method: The protocol likely uses quantum error correction and entanglement distillation techniques, possibly leveraging surface codes or similar topological codes, to distill high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from many noisy physical Bell pairs while minimizing spacetime overhead and requiring only 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with low spacetime cost, making it practical for distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: This work provides a resource-efficient method for generating logical Bell pairs, which is a key step towards scalable distributed quantum computing.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads to make quantum computing more practical.
method: The authors introduce a scheme that leverages good quantum LDPC codes, which have constant encoding rate and linear distance, combined with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to achieve efficient fault tolerance.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving over previous approaches. It demonstrates that fault-tolerant quantum computation can be performed with reduced resource requirements.
conclusion: The work advances the field of quantum error correction and fault tolerance by providing a more efficient architecture, which is a core focus in quantum information.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates it experimentally on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete framework for such certification.
method: They develop a new semidefinite programming hierarchy that fully characterizes the set of measurements simulable by projective ones, and implement it in a trapped-ion experiment.
result: The hierarchy provides a complete certification method, and the experimental demonstration validates its practical applicability.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for device-independent protocols and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, quantifying the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental thermodynamic constraints on quantum measurement, with implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with applications in quantum computing.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer exponential speedups for this task, potentially enabling new practical applications.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams, providing a rigorous complexity analysis.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over the best known classical algorithms for certain instances of the persistence computation problem, with provable guarantees.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a significant quantum advantage for a practical problem in data analysis, highlighting the potential of quantum computing in machine learning and data science.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters that enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement, with experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: The goal is to address the challenge of controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles in solid-state platforms, which are promising for quantum information processing but suffer from disorder and limited scalability.
method: The authors develop a control framework that leverages the inhomogeneity of spin ensembles to perform global operations and generate optically heralded entanglement, likely using techniques such as dynamical decoupling or optimal control.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement generation, with experimental overhead characterized for systems of 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a viable path towards programmable quantum matter using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, potentially enabling large-scale quantum networks or simulators.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of the continuous-variable approach to quantum communication, highlighting its advantages and recent developments.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical foundations, protocols (e.g., QKD, entanglement distribution), security proofs, and experimental implementations of continuous-variable quantum communication.
result: The review consolidates the state of the art, showing that continuous-variable techniques are mature and competitive with discrete-variable approaches.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a viable and promising direction for practical quantum networks, with ongoing advances in security and technology.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a structured overview of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, highlighting the potential and limitations of various primitives.
method: The paper classifies quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It offers a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and assesses their practical feasibility with current technology.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges that need to be addressed.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Sampling Of Pauli Strings For Nonstabilizerness
authors: Zhenyu Xiao And Shinsei Ryu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Xiao and Shinsei Ryu

Quantum magic, quantified by nonstabilizerness, measures departures from stabilizer structure and underlies potential quantum speedups. We introduce an efficient classical framework for computing stabilizer Rényi entropies and stabilizer nullity of generic [MATH]-qubit wave functions. The method combin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070402] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient classical framework for computing stabilizer Rényi entropies and stabilizer nullity, exponentially accelerating the sampling of Pauli strings for nonstabilizerness quantification.
motivation: Quantum magic (nonstabilizerness) is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its computation is often inefficient. The authors aim to provide a scalable classical method to compute these measures for generic many-qubit states.
method: The method combines a classical framework with efficient sampling of Pauli strings, likely using Monte Carlo or tensor network techniques, to estimate stabilizer Rényi entropies and nullity without exponential overhead.
result: The framework achieves exponential acceleration in sampling Pauli strings, enabling computation of nonstabilizerness for larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantifying quantum magic, which is relevant to quantum information theory and resource theories.

title: Quantum Advantage For Single-Photon State Characterization
authors: S. N. van Den Hoven, M. C. Anguita, S. Marzban, And J. J. Renema
abstract:
Author(s): S. N. van den Hoven, M. C. Anguita, S. Marzban, and J. J. Renema

We propose a multiphoton interference protocol that characterizes the pairwise overlaps of the internal modes of single photons more efficiently than pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel characterization experiments. We experimentally implement this protocol to characterize three photons. We show that our implem…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 073604] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a multiphoton interference protocol that characterizes pairwise overlaps of single-photon internal modes more efficiently than standard Hong-Ou-Mandel measurements.
motivation: Characterizing single-photon indistinguishability is crucial for quantum information processing, but pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel measurements scale inefficiently with photon number. A more efficient protocol is needed.
method: The authors design a multiphoton interference protocol that extracts pairwise overlaps from a single measurement, and implement it experimentally for three photons.
result: The protocol achieves higher efficiency than pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel characterization, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: This work provides a practical advantage in single-photon state characterization, relevant to quantum information applications.

title: Geometric And Resource-theoretic Characterization Of Nonstabilizerness In Quantum Algorithms
authors: Tom Krueger And Wolfgang Mauerer
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Krueger and Wolfgang Mauerer

While there is strong evidence for advantages of quantum over classical computation, the repertoire of computational primitives with proven or conjectured quantum advantage remains limited. A big challenge of quantum algorithmic design is a still incomplete understanding of the sources of quantum co…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022421] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a geometric and resource-theoretic characterization of nonstabilizerness (magic) in quantum algorithms, linking it to quantum information theory.
motivation: Understanding the sources of quantum advantage is incomplete; nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum computation, and its characterization can clarify algorithmic power.
method: The authors develop a geometric framework and resource-theoretic measures for nonstabilizerness, analyzing how it manifests in quantum algorithms.
result: They provide new characterizations and possibly bounds on nonstabilizerness, offering insights into the role of magic in quantum speedups.
conclusion: The work advances the resource theory of magic, which is relevant to quantum information theory and may guide algorithm design.

title: Developing A Universal Logical State-purification Strategy
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(de), And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(De), and Amit Kumar Pal

We develop a measurement-based protocol for purifying logical states of a quantum system, including quantum error correcting codes, in arbitrary thermal states with unit fidelity and finite probability, using a single auxiliary qubit. The protocol entails a time evolution caused by an engineered Ham…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022608] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a measurement-based protocol for purifying logical states of quantum error correcting codes from thermal states using a single auxiliary qubit, achieving unit fidelity with finite probability.
motivation: Logical states of quantum error correcting codes are typically prepared in pure states, but in practice they may be in thermal states due to finite temperature. Purifying these states is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The protocol uses an engineered Hamiltonian to evolve the system and a single auxiliary qubit, followed by a measurement on the auxiliary qubit. The purification is probabilistic but achieves unit fidelity when successful.
result: The protocol purifies logical states from arbitrary thermal states with unit fidelity and finite probability, and is applicable to various quantum error correcting codes.
conclusion: The proposed purification strategy provides a universal method to obtain pure logical states from thermal states, which is essential for practical quantum information processing.

title: Defect In Diamond With Millisecond-scale Spin Relaxation Time At Room Temperature
authors: Sounak Mukherjee, Anran Li, Johannes Eberle, Sean Karg, Zi-Huai Zhang, Mayer M. Feldman, Yilin Chen, Mark E. Turiansky, Mengen Wang, Yogendra Limbu, Tharnier O. abstract:
Author(s): Sounak Mukherjee, Anran Li, Johannes Eberle, Sean Karg, Zi-Huai Zhang, Mayer M. Feldman, Yilin Chen, Mark E. Turiansky, Mengen Wang, Yogendra Limbu, Tharnier O. Puel, Yueguang Shi, Matthew L. Markham, Rajesh L. Patel, Patryk Gumann, Michael E. Flatté, Chris G. Van de Walle, Stephen A. Lyon, and Nathalie P. de Leon

Nitrogen-vacancy centers and substitutional nitrogen (P1 centers) in diamond have until now been the only solid-state electron spin defects known to reach millisecond spin relaxation times (T
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074105] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a new defect in diamond (WAR5) with millisecond-scale spin relaxation time at room temperature, potentially useful for quantum sensing and networking.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin defects with long coherence times for quantum applications, as only NV and P1 centers were previously known to have millisecond T1 at room temperature.
method: The authors characterize the spin dynamics and optical spin polarization of the WAR5 defect, hypothesizing it to be the neutral oxygen vacancy center, using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: The WAR5 defect exhibits a T1 of ~1 ms at room temperature, rising to ~14 minutes at 4 K, among the longest for any solid-state spin defect.
conclusion: This new defect could serve as a promising platform for quantum sensing and networking, expanding the toolkit of solid-state spin systems.

title: Robust Tripartite Entanglement Generation Via Correlated Noise In Spin Qubits
authors: Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

We investigate the generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system due to spatially correlated noise. In particular, we demonstrate how the formation of a highly entangled dark state, a [MATH] state, enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement. Surprisingly, we fi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033153] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system via spatially correlated noise, leveraging a dark state to achieve long-lived entanglement.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how correlated noise, typically detrimental, can be harnessed to generate and stabilize multipartite entanglement in spin qubit systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: They theoretically analyze a triangular spin-qubit system under spatially correlated noise, showing that the noise drives the system into a dark state that is highly entangled, and they study the robustness and lifetime of this entanglement.
result: They find that the dark state formation enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement, and surprisingly, the entanglement persists even when the noise is not perfectly correlated.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for generating multipartite entanglement using noise, which could be exploited in quantum networks and quantum information tasks.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for inferring quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.
motivation: Validating large-scale quantum simulations is crucial, and existing methods often lack rigorous error bounds. The authors aim to provide a systematic approach to infer Hamiltonians and Lindbladians from experimental data with certified accuracy.
method: The framework combines Hamiltonian and Lindbladian learning techniques with statistical inference to extract model parameters and compute rigorous error bounds from experimental measurements.
result: The framework is demonstrated on a trapped-ion quantum simulator, showing that it can accurately infer the underlying dynamics and provide tight error bounds, thus validating the simulation.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical and rigorous method for certifying quantum simulations, which is essential for reliable quantum computing and simulation.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived molecular spins detected via mechanical readout, enabling nanotesla magnetic field sensing and local nuclear spectra resolution.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity quantum sensing with long coherence times, integrating molecular spins with mechanical detection offers a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator for readout, likely using magnetic resonance force microscopy techniques.
result: They detect nanotesla-level magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, showcasing the sensitivity and resolution of the hybrid system.
conclusion: The work establishes molecular spins with mechanical readout as a viable platform for quantum sensing, with potential applications in nanoscale imaging and spectroscopy.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom processor, which is a key platform in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The processor simulates the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely using a Rydberg atom array or similar platform, and quantifies the computational advantage through benchmarking against classical simulations.
result: The experiment shows a clear quantum computational advantage, with the quantum processor outperforming classical methods in simulating the entangled dynamics.
conclusion: This work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for demonstrating quantum advantage, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a no-go theorem showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group for multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires implementing logical gates, but certain gadget constructions may have fundamental limitations. Understanding these limitations is crucial for designing scalable quantum computers.
method: The authors analyze common classes of fault-tolerant gadgets and prove a no-go theorem using group-theoretic and coding-theoretic arguments.
result: They show that these gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group, implying a trade-off between fault tolerance and gate universality.
conclusion: The result guides future fault-tolerant designs by highlighting the need for alternative approaches to achieve universal quantum computation.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational complexity, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors analyze noisy 2D random circuits, likely using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior under noise.
result: They find that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.
conclusion: The results highlight the fragility of measurement-induced entanglement to noise, which is important for understanding the limits of quantum advantage and the design of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: To enhance the performance of hybrid quantum systems by understanding and mitigating loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits.
method: The authors systematically optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize the resulting phonon coherence times and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence time and cooperativity, and identify key loss mechanisms, leading to a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The findings provide a clear path for engineering high-coherence mechanical resonators for quantum information processing, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
