Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and revealing connections to quantum error correction and entanglement transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for quantum error correction and fault tolerance. The authors aim to characterize the decodability of monitored quantum codes and its relation to measurement statistics.
method: The paper likely uses theoretical analysis of monitored quantum circuits, possibly employing statistical mechanics mappings, entanglement measures, and decoding protocols to analyze the effect of random measurements on code properties.
result: The authors find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they provide new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics and its implications for quantum error correction, suggesting that measurement outcomes can be leveraged to improve decoding in quantum codes.

title: Pre-distillation Of Magic States Via Composite Schemes
authors: Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, And Haim Suchowski
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, and Haim Suchowski

Magic state distillation (MSD) is a cornerstone of fault-tolerant quantum computing, enabling non-Clifford gates via state injection into stabilizer circuits. However, the substantial overhead of current MSD protocols remains a major obstacle to scalable implementations. We propose a general framewo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022415] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general framework for pre-distilling magic states via composite schemes to reduce the overhead of magic state distillation.
motivation: Magic state distillation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but suffers from high overhead, hindering scalability.
method: The authors introduce a composite scheme framework that combines multiple distillation protocols or pre-processing steps to improve efficiency.
result: The framework demonstrates reduced overhead compared to standard MSD protocols, as shown in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed composite schemes offer a promising path to more efficient magic state distillation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Classical Optimization Of Reduced Density Matrix Estimations With Classical Shadows Using $N$-representability Conditions Under Shot Noise Considerations
authors: Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, And Michael Streif
abstract:
Author(s): Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, and Michael Streif

Classical shadow tomography has become a powerful tool in learning about quantum states prepared on a quantum computer. Recent works have used classical shadows to variationally enforce [MATH]-representability conditions on the two-particle reduced density matrix. In this paper, we build upon previous …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033167] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes classical shadow tomography for estimating two-particle reduced density matrices by enforcing N-representability conditions, improving accuracy under shot noise.
motivation: Classical shadow tomography is a powerful tool for learning quantum states, but estimating reduced density matrices (RDMs) can be inefficient. Enforcing N-representability conditions can improve accuracy, but previous methods may not be optimal under shot noise.
method: The authors propose a classical optimization approach that incorporates N-representability constraints into the estimation of two-particle RDMs from classical shadows, explicitly considering shot noise effects.
result: The method demonstrates improved accuracy in estimating RDMs compared to standard approaches, particularly in the presence of shot noise, as shown in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a practical enhancement to classical shadow tomography for quantum chemistry and other applications, making RDM estimation more reliable with limited measurements.

title: Highly Robust Logical Qubit Encoding In An Ensemble Of V-symmetrical Qutrits
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, And Julio Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, and Julio Guerrero

We propose using even and odd Schrödinger cat states formed from coherent states of U(3) of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration (a qubit-disguised qutrit) to encode a logical qubit. These carefully engineered logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033169] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes encoding a logical qubit in even and odd Schrödinger cat states of U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of V-symmetrical qutrits, which are parameter-independent stationary states.
motivation: To find robust encodings of logical qubits that are resilient to errors, using the structure of qutrit ensembles with V-symmetry.
method: The authors construct even and odd cat states from U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of qutrits in a V configuration, and analyze their properties as logical qubit encodings.
result: The proposed logical qubit states are stationary and parameter-independent, suggesting robustness against certain types of noise.
conclusion: The encoding offers a promising approach for robust quantum information processing using qutrit ensembles.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature properties, such as extensive entanglement, challenging conventional notions of ground states.
motivation: To explore the possibility of realizing infinite-temperature-like behavior in the ground state of local Hamiltonians, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors design specific local Hamiltonians and analyze their ground states, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to demonstrate extensive entanglement and other infinite-temperature signatures.
result: They show that these Hamiltonians have ground states with extensive entanglement, mimicking properties of infinite-temperature states despite being at zero energy.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of Hamiltonians with exotic ground states, potentially relevant for understanding thermalization and quantum information in many-body systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent time evolution simulation, which achieves better query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus compared to gradient-descent approaches.
motivation: Quantum optimization often suffers from barren plateaus and high query complexity in gradient-based methods. The authors aim to develop a more efficient and robust optimization technique for variational quantum algorithms.
method: The method uses coherent simulation of time evolution to compute parameter updates without gradients, leveraging the dynamics of the quantum system to guide the optimization.
result: The proposed approach demonstrates improved query complexity and resilience to barren plateaus in numerical experiments, outperforming gradient-descent-based methods.
conclusion: The gradient-free dynamical simulation approach offers a promising alternative for quantum optimization, potentially enhancing the practicality of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation that achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and reducing its overhead is crucial for practical implementations. The authors aim to improve efficiency for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, which are relevant for certain quantum computing platforms.
method: The paper proposes a fold-transversal approach to surface code cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to reduce spacetime overhead. It likely involves a combination of code design and protocol optimization.
result: The new strategy achieves low spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, as demonstrated through analysis or simulations.
conclusion: The proposed cultivation strategy offers a practical advantage for quantum computing architectures with nonlocal connectivity, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in continual quantum learning, showing that quantum neural networks maintain learning flexibility even as parameters grow.
motivation: Continual learning in classical neural networks suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and the authors aim to explore whether quantum neural networks offer advantages in this context.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, likely using theoretical arguments and numerical simulations to demonstrate plasticity preservation.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, allowing them to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones, unlike classical counterparts.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks may provide a natural solution to catastrophic forgetting, with implications for quantum machine learning and resource theories.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, achieving high decoding accuracy with low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements or demand massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm tailored to QLDPC codes, which explores a limited set of candidate error patterns in a breadth-first manner, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time operation, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of QLDPC codes, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: The goal is to enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum computers.
method: The authors design 'twisted color circuits' that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, and they develop a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance, as demonstrated through analysis and likely simulations.
conclusion: This work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a practical approach for non-Clifford gates on a planar architecture.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and sampling tasks, but previous results were often architecture-specific or limited to asymptotic depths.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of the local noise and circuit architecture, deriving universal formulas for the anticoncentration measure as a function of depth and noise strength.
result: They identify distinct regimes (e.g., noise-dominated, circuit-dominated) and show that anticoncentration is universal across different architectures, with a crossover depth that depends on noise and connectivity.
conclusion: The findings provide a unified framework for predicting anticoncentration in practical noisy circuits, with implications for quantum advantage experiments and benchmarking.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity has been lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they derive bounds and examples.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a new fundamental tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on quantum sensing near quantum phase transitions, focusing on parameter estimation and the use of criticality to surpass classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions offer divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for highly sensitive parameter estimation, potentially surpassing classical limits. The tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to this emerging field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations of critical quantum sensing, covering concepts such as quantum Fisher information, critical exponents, and various physical platforms.
result: It consolidates known results and techniques, highlighting the potential of criticality for enhanced metrology and discussing challenges and open questions.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision measurements, and this tutorial serves as a valuable resource for researchers entering the field.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the three-level Toffoli gate.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages in quantum computing, such as reducing circuit complexity and enabling more efficient gate decompositions, which could improve quantum algorithm implementation.
method: The paper surveys various qudit-qubit embeddings, discusses theoretical frameworks for gate decomposition using qudits, and reviews current experimental demonstrations of qudit-based quantum computing.
result: It shows that qudits can drastically simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and provides an overview of experimental progress in qudit-based quantum information processing.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, offering practical benefits in gate decomposition and algorithm realization, though further development is needed for widespread adoption.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical features of gravity.
motivation: To address the fundamental question of whether gravity is classical or quantum by using information-theoretic methods and feasible experiments.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale experiments.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete analyses of potentially feasible GIE experiments.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete way to constrain theories of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue.

title: Equivalence Between Exponential Concentration In Quantum Machine Learning Kernels And Barren Plateaus In Variational Algorithms
authors: Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, And Roman V. Krems
abstract:
Author(s): Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, and Roman V. Krems

We show that a parametrized quantum neural network can be used to build a nonparametric quantum kernel for machine learning that inherits the concentration properties of the neural network cost function. This construction establishes a rigorous connection between barren plateaus (BPs) in variational…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022417] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of quantum machine learning, particularly the concentration of kernel values and barren plateaus, is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors construct a nonparametric quantum kernel from a parametrized quantum neural network and prove that the concentration properties of the kernel are directly inherited from the network's cost function.
result: They demonstrate that exponential concentration in the kernel is equivalent to the presence of barren plateaus in the variational algorithm, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: This connection implies that avoiding barren plateaus is necessary to prevent exponential concentration in quantum kernels, guiding the design of quantum machine learning models.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes, providing universal signatures of quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics. The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic, but its analytic calculation beyond leading order has been challenging.
method: The authors employ a diagrammatic approach and random matrix theory to compute the spectral form factor analytically, extending the calculation to second order in time and covering all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal corrections that depend on the symmetry class and the structure of the many-body system.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and its universal signatures, with implications for thermalization and the information-theoretic aspects of quantum dynamics.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To provide a practical tool for quantifying and detecting magic in mixed states, which is crucial for quantum computing and resource theories.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on convexity and set properties, analogous to entanglement criteria, and apply it to magic state distillation and detection.
result: The criterion enables detection of nonstabilizerness and certification of undistillability for certain mixed states, with applications in magic state distillation.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a new, simple approach to studying magic resources, potentially advancing quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Non-Markovian Hatano-Nelson Model
authors: Sumit Kumar Jana, Ryo Hanai, Tan van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa, And Archak Purkayastha
abstract:
Author(s): Sumit Kumar Jana, Ryo Hanai, Tan Van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa, and Archak Purkayastha

While considering non-Hermitian Hamiltonians arising in the presence of dissipation, in most cases, the dissipation is taken to be frequency-independent. However, this idealization may not always be applicable in experimental settings, where dissipation can be frequency-dependent. Such frequency-dep…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070404] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson model with frequency-dependent dissipation, revealing non-Markovian effects that alter the localization transition and steady-state properties.
motivation: Most studies of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians assume frequency-independent dissipation, which may not hold experimentally. The authors aim to explore the impact of frequency-dependent dissipation on the Hatano-Nelson model, a paradigmatic system for non-Hermitian physics.
method: They formulate a non-Markovian quantum master equation and derive an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with frequency-dependent terms. They analyze the spectrum and steady states, possibly using numerical and analytical techniques.
result: The frequency-dependent dissipation leads to a modified localization transition and non-Markovian dynamics that cannot be captured by standard Markovian approximations. The steady state exhibits features distinct from the Markovian case.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of non-Markovian effects in non-Hermitian quantum systems and provides a framework for understanding dissipation in realistic settings.

title: Emergent Decoherence Dynamics In Doubly Disordered Spin Networks
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, Zhuorui Zhang, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, Zhuorui Zhang, and Ashok Ajoy

Elucidating the emergence of irreversible macroscopic laws from reversible quantum many-body dynamics remains challenging, particularly in disordered media. Here, in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, we uncover an emergent decoherence law for $^{13}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070803] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals an emergent decoherence law in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, linking microscopic disorder to macroscopic irreversibility.
motivation: Understanding how irreversible macroscopic laws emerge from reversible quantum dynamics is a fundamental challenge, especially in disordered media. The authors aim to uncover universal decoherence behavior in a realistic spin network.
method: They study a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, likely using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling to characterize the decoherence dynamics of 13C nuclear spins.
result: They discover an emergent decoherence law that captures the interplay of disorder and interactions, providing insights into the onset of irreversibility.
conclusion: The findings advance our understanding of decoherence in disordered spin systems, with implications for quantum sensing and memory applications in diamond-based platforms.

title: Joint Parameter Estimation And Multidimensional Reconciliation For Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Jisheng Dai, Xue-Qin Jiang, Peng Huang, Tao Wang, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Jisheng Dai, Xue-Qin Jiang, Peng Huang, Tao Wang, and Guihua Zeng

Accurate quantum channel parameter estimation is essential for effective information reconciliation in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD). However, conventional maximum likelihood (ML) estimators rely on a large amount of disclosed data, leading to a significant loss in symbol eff…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022429] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a joint parameter estimation and multidimensional reconciliation method for CV-QKD to reduce symbol loss and improve key rate.
motivation: Conventional ML estimators for CV-QKD require large disclosed data, causing significant symbol loss. The authors aim to improve efficiency by jointly estimating parameters and performing reconciliation.
method: They develop a joint estimation and reconciliation scheme that integrates parameter estimation with multidimensional reconciliation, likely using a modified ML estimator or iterative approach.
result: The method reduces the amount of disclosed data needed for parameter estimation, thereby increasing the effective symbol efficiency and key rate in CV-QKD.
conclusion: Joint parameter estimation and reconciliation can enhance the performance of CV-QKD systems by reducing overhead and improving key rates.

title: Implementation Of A Hybrid Tripartite Interaction Between A Two-level Atom And Two Cavities In The Strong-driving Regime
authors: Tong Liu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Bao-Qing Guo, Qi-Cheng Wu, Dong-Xu Chen, And Chui-Ping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Liu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Bao-Qing Guo, Qi-Cheng Wu, Dong-Xu Chen, and Chui-Ping Yang

Tripartite interactions have recently garnered significant interest owing to their potential in quantum information processing and quantum computation. In this work, we present a scheme for realizing a hybrid tripartite interaction between an atom and two cavities in the strong-driving regime. This …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023715] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a hybrid tripartite interaction between a two-level atom and two cavities in the strong-driving regime, which could be useful for quantum information processing.
motivation: Tripartite interactions are important for quantum information processing, but implementing them in hybrid systems is challenging. The authors aim to provide a feasible scheme using strong driving to simplify the experimental requirements.
method: The scheme uses a two-level atom coupled to two cavities, with strong driving fields applied to the cavities. By appropriately tuning the driving strengths and detunings, an effective tripartite interaction is engineered, as analyzed via a unitary transformation and effective Hamiltonian.
result: The paper shows that the proposed scheme can generate a hybrid tripartite interaction with high fidelity under realistic parameters, and discusses the effects of decoherence and parameter imperfections.
conclusion: The scheme offers a promising approach to realize tripartite interactions in hybrid quantum systems, potentially enabling applications in quantum information processing and quantum computation.

title: Physical Origins Of Shortest Control Time From Feasibility Boundaries In Quantum Control
authors: I-Yun Hsiao And Yoshiaki Teranishi
abstract:
Author(s): I-Yun Hsiao and Yoshiaki Teranishi

We study quantum controllability under finite control resources using a multiobjective optimization perspective. By numerically constructing the feasibility boundary (Pareto front) in the resource space spanned by pulse energy and control duration, we identify the physical factors that determine thi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022614] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies physical factors determining the shortest control time in quantum control by analyzing feasibility boundaries in resource space.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on quantum control speed under finite resources, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: Uses a multiobjective optimization perspective to numerically construct Pareto fronts in the resource space of pulse energy and control duration.
result: Identifies physical factors that determine the shortest control time, likely related to energy-time uncertainty and controllability constraints.
conclusion: Provides insights into the trade-offs between control resources and speed, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Transient-energy-backflow-enhanced Ergotropy In An Open Qubit Quantum Battery Assisted By An Auxiliary Oscillator
authors: Shun-Cai Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shun-Cai Zhao

Decoherence and dissipation in open quantum systems generally drive quantum batteries toward passive states, thereby reducing their extractable work (ergotropy). Here, we study a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator in the presence of dephasing and diss…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023106] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven qubit quantum battery coupled to an auxiliary oscillator, showing that transient energy backflow can enhance ergotropy despite decoherence.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from decoherence and dissipation, which reduce extractable work. The authors aim to find mechanisms to mitigate this degradation.
method: They model a driven qubit battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator under dephasing and dissipation, and analyze the dynamics of ergotropy.
result: They find that transient energy backflow from the auxiliary oscillator to the battery can enhance ergotropy, counteracting the detrimental effects of decoherence.
conclusion: The auxiliary oscillator provides a practical way to improve quantum battery performance, offering insights into energy storage in open quantum systems.

title: Directional Charging Of Topological Quantum Energy-storage Devices Driven By The non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, And Hongrong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, and Hongrong Li

The skin effect is a phenomenon characterized by the exponential localization of wave functions at a boundary in non-Hermitian topological systems, demonstrating potential applications in the field of quantum information. Here we explore its application in optimizing the performance of quantum energ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023712] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using the non-Hermitian skin effect to directionally charge quantum energy storage devices, enhancing charging efficiency.
motivation: Quantum energy storage (e.g., quantum batteries) is a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and improving charging performance is of practical interest.
method: The authors theoretically model a quantum energy storage device in a non-Hermitian topological system, exploiting the skin effect to achieve directional charging.
result: They demonstrate that the skin effect enables efficient and controllable charging, potentially outperforming conventional schemes.
conclusion: The non-Hermitian skin effect offers a novel mechanism for optimizing quantum energy storage, contributing to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Noise Tolerance Via Reinforcement In The Quantum Search Problem
authors: Marjan Homayouni-Sangari And Abolfazl Ramezanpour
abstract:
Author(s): Marjan Homayouni-Sangari and Abolfazl Ramezanpour

The Grover lower bound for the unstructured search problem can be surpassed when some information about the data structure is available. Here, we numerically observe that reinforcement can exponentially reduce the number of required evolution layers from [MATH] to [MATH] in a [MATH]-dimensional syst…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022423] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that reinforcement learning can exponentially reduce the number of evolution layers needed in Grover's quantum search algorithm when partial information about the data structure is available, improving noise tolerance.
motivation: The Grover lower bound for unstructured search can be surpassed with structural information, and the authors aim to exploit this via reinforcement to reduce circuit depth and enhance noise tolerance.
method: They numerically simulate a quantum search algorithm with reinforcement learning to adaptively choose evolution layers, comparing the required number of layers with and without reinforcement in the presence of noise.
result: Reinforcement reduces the number of required layers from exponential to polynomial (or logarithmic) in system dimension, significantly improving noise tolerance.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a practical way to mitigate noise in quantum search by reducing circuit depth, potentially advancing quantum algorithms for near-term devices.

title: $\mathit{In}$ situ Rewiring Of Two-dimensional Ion Lattice Interactions Using Metastable State Shelving
authors: Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, And Philip Richerme
abstract:
Author(s): Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, and Philip Richerme

Trapped-ion lattice geometries, which determine the interactions between trapped-ion qubits, are typically governed by the balance of Coulomb repulsion forces with the external trapping potential. Here we demonstrate how the effective ion lattice geometry and resulting qubit-qubit interactions may b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022425] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates in-situ rewiring of trapped-ion lattice interactions using metastable state shelving, enabling dynamic control of qubit-qubit couplings.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum simulators typically have fixed lattice geometries, limiting their flexibility. The authors aim to dynamically control ion interactions to enable more versatile quantum simulations.
method: They use metastable state shelving to selectively alter the effective trapping potential for certain ions, thereby changing the lattice geometry and interaction strengths in real time.
result: They experimentally demonstrate rewiring of the ion lattice and show that the resulting qubit-qubit interactions can be tuned, as evidenced by changes in spin-spin coupling.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for dynamically programming trapped-ion quantum simulators, expanding their capability to simulate a wider range of Hamiltonians.

title: Agnostic Parameter Estimation With Large Spins
authors: Huining Zhang And X. X. Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Huining Zhang and X. X. Yi

The quantum Fisher information of a quantum state with respect to a certain parameter quantifies the sensitivity of the quantum state to changes in that parameter. Maximizing the quantum Fisher information is essential for achieving the optimal estimation precision of quantum sensors. A typical quan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022612] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies agnostic parameter estimation with large spins, focusing on maximizing quantum Fisher information without prior knowledge of the probe state.
motivation: Quantum sensors often require optimizing quantum Fisher information, but typical approaches assume knowledge of the probe state. This work addresses the agnostic scenario where the state is unknown, which is more realistic.
method: The authors analyze parameter estimation using large spin systems, deriving bounds and strategies for maximizing quantum Fisher information in an agnostic setting, likely using spin coherent states and quantum metrology techniques.
result: They provide results on achievable precision and optimal measurements for large spin probes, possibly showing advantages or limitations compared to known-state scenarios.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum metrology by extending parameter estimation to agnostic settings with large spins, offering practical guidance for quantum sensors.

title: Robust Two-qubit Gates For Semiconductor Spin Qubits Based On Dynamical Dimensionality Reduction
authors: Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, And Zheng-Yuan Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, and Zheng-Yuan Xue

High-fidelity two-qubit gates leverage qubit-qubit interactions and are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, environmental noise and imperfect control of the interactions are inevitable, which degrade the quality of gate operations. Here we introduce local microwave driving in conven…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022613] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a robust two-qubit gate scheme for semiconductor spin qubits using dynamical dimensionality reduction to suppress noise and imperfect control.
motivation: High-fidelity two-qubit gates are essential for scalable quantum computing, but environmental noise and imperfect control degrade gate quality. The authors aim to improve gate robustness in semiconductor spin qubits.
method: They introduce local microwave driving in a conventional two-qubit gate setup and apply dynamical dimensionality reduction to design pulses that are robust against noise and control errors.
result: The proposed scheme achieves high-fidelity two-qubit gates with significantly improved robustness compared to conventional methods, as demonstrated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to enhance two-qubit gate performance in semiconductor spin qubits, contributing to the development of scalable quantum computation.

title: Tabletop Reversibility Of Phase-covariant Operations
authors: Fangzhen Chen And Xueyuan Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Fangzhen Chen and Xueyuan Hu

Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are both fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and it is of great importance to study the interplay between them. In this paper, we study tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant quantum operations and obtain sharply different conclusions for fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022419] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies tabletop reversibility of phase-covariant quantum operations, revealing a sharp contrast between finite and infinite dimensions.
motivation: Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and understanding their interplay is important.
method: The authors analyze tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant operations, deriving conditions for reversibility in finite and infinite dimensions.
result: They find that TTR holds for all phase-covariant operations in finite dimensions but fails in infinite dimensions, with specific counterexamples.
conclusion: The results highlight the role of dimension in reversibility of quantum operations and contribute to the theory of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Coherence And Entanglement In Wireless Quantum Batteries
authors: Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, and Dong Wang

We investigate the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system mediated by a common structured bosonic environment. By employing a unified resource-theoretic analysis, we elucidate the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022420] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of wireless quantum batteries, focusing on the roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a promising application of quantum thermodynamics, and understanding how environmental memory and symmetry affect their performance is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors employ a unified resource-theoretic analysis to study a wireless quantum battery system mediated by a common structured bosonic environment, analyzing the interplay of quantum coherence and entanglement.
result: They elucidate distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in the charging process and thermodynamic efficiency, showing how these factors influence battery performance.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into optimizing quantum battery designs by leveraging environmental memory and symmetry, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Giant-atom Quantum Battery
authors: Lei Qiao And P. Z. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Qiao and P. Z. Zhao

Most studies of quantum batteries have been restricted to conventional atoms whose size is much smaller than the electromagnetic modes. Here we propose a scheme for a quantum battery based on giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide. Specifically, both the charger and the battery are giant atoms…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022205] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum battery scheme using giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide, exploring its charging and energy storage properties.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and most studies use conventional atoms. This work aims to exploit the unique properties of giant atoms to improve battery performance.
method: The authors model a quantum battery where both charger and battery are giant atoms coupled to a common waveguide, and analyze the dynamics of energy transfer and storage.
result: They find that the giant-atom configuration allows for efficient charging and stable energy storage, with performance depending on the coupling strengths and detunings.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom quantum battery offers a promising alternative to conventional designs, potentially enhancing the practicality of quantum batteries.

title: Minimal-energy Optimal Control Of Tunable Two-qubit Gates In Superconducting Platforms Using Continuous Dynamical Decoupling
authors: Adonai Hilário Da Silva, Octávio Da Motta, Leonardo K. Castelano, And Reginaldo de Jesus Napolitano
abstract:
Author(s): Adonai Hilário da Silva, Octávio da Motta, Leonardo K. Castelano, and Reginaldo de Jesus Napolitano

We present a unified scheme for generating high-fidelity entangling gates in superconducting platforms by continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) combined with variational minimal-energy optimal control. During the CDD stage, we suppress residual couplings, calibration drifting, and quasistatic noise,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022606] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a unified scheme for high-fidelity entangling gates in superconducting platforms using continuous dynamical decoupling and minimal-energy optimal control.
motivation: To improve the fidelity and robustness of two-qubit gates in superconducting qubits, which are crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors combine continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to suppress noise and residual couplings with variational minimal-energy optimal control to design gate pulses that minimize energy while maintaining high fidelity.
result: The scheme achieves high-fidelity entangling gates with reduced sensitivity to noise and calibration errors, and demonstrates energy savings compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a practical and efficient way to implement robust two-qubit gates in superconducting platforms, advancing the development of reliable quantum processors.

title: Engineering Quantum Mpemba Effect By Liouvillian Skin Effect
authors: Xiang Zhang, Chen Sun, And Fuxiang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Zhang, Chen Sun, and Fuxiang Li

We propose an approach to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—wherein an initial state farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one—using the Liouvillian skin effect (LSE) in open quantum systems. In an open quantum chain with LSE, we show that the QME can be readily achieved simpl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084305] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes engineering the quantum Mpemba effect using the Liouvillian skin effect in open quantum systems, demonstrating faster relaxation for states farther from equilibrium.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and control. The authors aim to provide a systematic method to engineer this effect in open quantum systems.
method: They consider an open quantum chain with the Liouvillian skin effect, where the non-Hermitian skin effect leads to a separation of relaxation timescales. They analyze the relaxation dynamics and show conditions under which the QME emerges.
result: They show that the QME can be readily achieved in such systems, with the relaxation rate depending on the initial state's overlap with certain eigenmodes. They provide a simple mechanism based on the Liouvillian spectrum.
conclusion: The work offers a practical route to engineer the QME, which may be useful for controlling relaxation in open quantum systems and has implications for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Control-driven Critical Fluctuations Across Quantum Trajectories
authors: Haining Pan, Thomas Iadecola, E. M. Stoudenmire, And J. H. Pixley
abstract:
Author(s): Haining Pan, Thomas Iadecola, E. M. Stoudenmire, and J. H. Pixley

Monitored quantum circuits in which entangling unitary dynamics compete with projective local measurements can host measurement-induced phase transitions witnessed by entanglement measures at late times. Adding feedback conditioned on the measurement outcomes gives rise to another type of phase tran…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074307] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-induced phase transitions in monitored quantum circuits with feedback, focusing on control-driven critical fluctuations across quantum trajectories.
motivation: To understand the role of feedback in monitored quantum circuits and how it affects entanglement phase transitions, which is a key topic in quantum information and many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with feedback using numerical simulations and possibly tensor network methods, examining entanglement measures and critical behavior.
result: They find that feedback can drive new types of phase transitions and critical fluctuations, extending the understanding of measurement-induced transitions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay of measurement, feedback, and entanglement, relevant for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Dynamics With Stationary Thermal States
authors: Adrián A. Budini
abstract:
Author(s): Adrián A. Budini

Quantum and classical systems can consistently be coupled via nonunitary time-irreversible mechanisms. In this paper, we characterize which kind of corresponding dynamics converge in the stationary regime to a thermal hybrid state, that is, a density matrix that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024125] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes hybrid quantum-classical dynamics that converge to thermal stationary states, linking nonunitary coupling to entropy maximization.
motivation: To understand how quantum and classical systems can be consistently coupled to reach thermal equilibrium, which is fundamental for hybrid quantum-classical thermodynamics.
method: The author analyzes nonunitary time-irreversible coupling mechanisms and derives conditions for the stationary state to be a thermal hybrid state that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entropy.
result: The paper identifies classes of dynamics that lead to thermal stationary states and provides a characterization of the corresponding entropy and equilibrium conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide a framework for constructing hybrid quantum-classical dynamics with well-defined thermal equilibria, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Framework For Fluctuating Times And Counting Observables In Stochastic Excursions
authors: Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, and Gabriel T. Landi

Many natural systems exhibit dynamics characterized by alternating phases or recurring sets of states. Describing the fluctuations of such systems over stochastic trajectories is necessary across diverse fields, from biological motors to quantum thermal machines. In an accompanying letter, we introd…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024129] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing fluctuations of times and counting observables in stochastic excursions, with applications to quantum thermal machines.
motivation: Many natural systems exhibit alternating phases or recurring states, and understanding fluctuations over stochastic trajectories is crucial for fields like biological motors and quantum thermal machines.
method: The authors introduce a theoretical framework based on stochastic excursions, likely using large deviation theory or counting statistics to characterize fluctuations of times and observables.
result: The framework provides a unified description of fluctuations in excursion times and counting observables, enabling analysis of thermodynamic quantities in non-equilibrium processes.
conclusion: The framework offers a versatile tool for studying fluctuations in stochastic systems, with potential applications to quantum thermodynamics and beyond.

title: Geometry-driven Thermodynamic Anomaly In Overdamped Langevin Dynamics
authors: Sehyeok Lee And Min Soo Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Sehyeok Lee and Min Soo Kim

Changing geometry creates its own overdamped thermodynamic anomaly. This is the geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped anomaly known for Langevin systems in nonuniform or time-dependent temperature fields. We show this for Langevin dynamics in [MATH] under a time-dependent potent…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024118] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped thermodynamic anomaly in overdamped Langevin dynamics with time-dependent potentials.
motivation: To explore how changing geometry affects thermodynamic behavior in overdamped Langevin systems, extending known anomalies to geometric settings.
method: The authors analyze overdamped Langevin dynamics under time-dependent potentials and derive thermodynamic quantities, identifying an anomaly induced by geometry.
result: They demonstrate that geometry alone can produce a thermodynamic anomaly analogous to the underdamped-overdamped case, with implications for stochastic thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of geometry in non-equilibrium thermodynamics, offering new insights into thermodynamic anomalies in stochastic systems.

title: Counting Observables In Stochastic Excursions
authors: Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, And Gabriel T. Landi
