Author(s): Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, and Gabriel T. Landi

Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields of research, from quantum thermal machines to biological motors. We introduce a framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories, dubbed stochastic excursions, of pr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022102] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for analyzing the statistics of counting observables in stochastic excursions, with applications to quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields, including quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories (stochastic excursions) of stochastic processes.
result: The framework provides a systematic way to compute statistics of counting observables in excursions, potentially revealing new fluctuation relations or bounds.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of fluctuations in stochastic processes, with implications for thermodynamics of small systems and information processing.

title: Thermalization Rates And Quantum Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances: Insights From Operator Hydrodynamics
authors: Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, And Curt von Keyserlingk
abstract:
Author(s): Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, and Curt von Keyserlingk

In thermalizing many-body quantum systems without conservation laws, such as ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, local expectation values are predicted to decay to their equilibrium values exponentially quickly. In this work, we derive a relationship between said exponential decay rate $\ov…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033186] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a relationship between thermalization rates and quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances using operator hydrodynamics, providing insights into exponential decay in ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits.
motivation: Understanding the exponential decay of local expectation values in thermalizing many-body quantum systems without conservation laws is a fundamental question in quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors employ operator hydrodynamics to analyze the spectral properties of the quantum channel, connecting the decay rate to quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances.
result: They establish a quantitative link between the thermalization rate and the leading resonance, offering a new perspective on the emergence of hydrodynamics in chaotic quantum systems.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of thermalization in quantum systems, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Intermodal Entanglement In A Quantum Optical Model Of High-harmonic Generation Due To The Backaction On The Driving Field
authors: Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, And Tamás Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, and Tamás Kiss

Preparation of nonclassical light with special quantum properties is essential for quantum technologies. High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a process that not only enables the creation of attosecond pulses but also has the potential to generate light with intricate quantum properties. In a recent exp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033154] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates intermodal entanglement in high-harmonic generation, showing that the backaction on the driving field can produce nonclassical correlations between harmonic modes.
motivation: High-harmonic generation is a promising source of nonclassical light for quantum technologies, and understanding its quantum properties is essential. The backaction of the driving field on the generated harmonics may lead to entanglement, which has not been fully explored.
method: The authors develop a quantum optical model of HHG that includes the backaction on the driving field, and analyze the resulting quantum state of the harmonic modes. They compute entanglement measures and study the dependence on parameters such as driving field intensity and harmonic order.
result: The model predicts the generation of intermodal entanglement between different harmonic modes, with the degree of entanglement depending on the driving field parameters. The backaction is crucial for the entanglement, as it correlates the modes.
conclusion: The results suggest that HHG can serve as a source of entangled multi-mode light, which could be useful for quantum information processing and quantum communication. The work provides a theoretical foundation for experimental exploration.

title: Propagation Of The Space-time Entanglement Of Twin Photons And Twin Beams
authors: Alessandra Gatti And Enrico Brambilla
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Gatti and Enrico Brambilla

We investigate how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs generated by multimode parametric down-conversion (PDC) propagates away from the source. We show that the entangled two-photon probability, tightly confined in space and time at the source, quickly broadens and decays out of a focal plan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033165] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs generated by parametric down-conversion propagates and broadens away from the source.
motivation: Understanding the propagation of spatial and temporal entanglement is crucial for quantum communication and imaging applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the two-photon probability distribution for multimode PDC, deriving expressions for its evolution in space and time.
result: They show that the entangled two-photon probability, initially tightly confined, broadens and decays out of the focal plane, with the entanglement structure changing with propagation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the spatial-temporal entanglement dynamics of PDC sources, relevant for quantum information protocols.

title: Controlling Emergent Dynamical Behavior Via Phase-engineered Strong Symmetries
authors: Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, And Parvinder Solanki
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, and Parvinder Solanki

Symmetry constraints provide a powerful means to control the dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the set of accessible control parameters is often limited. Here, we show that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces a phase-dependent strong symmet…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033166] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces phase-dependent strong symmetries, enabling control over emergent dynamical behavior.
motivation: Symmetry constraints are powerful for controlling open quantum systems, but accessible control parameters are often limited. The authors aim to expand control by exploiting a tunable phase in the coupling.
method: They analyze a cavity QED system with a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling, showing that this phase gives rise to phase-dependent strong symmetries. They likely use theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting dynamics.
result: The phase-dependent strong symmetries allow for control of emergent dynamical behavior, such as steady-state selection or dynamical phases, in the open quantum system.
conclusion: The work provides a new control knob for open quantum systems via phase-engineered symmetries, with potential applications in quantum technology.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase observable only through joint measurement.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems, and its experimental realization in a controllable platform like trapped ions is of high interest.
method: The authors engineer dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, and measure the synchronized state via joint measurements.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, contributing to the understanding of quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for simulating quantum systems using Pauli propagation, covering theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Efficient simulation of quantum systems is crucial for understanding and developing quantum technologies, and Pauli propagation offers a promising approach.
method: The authors develop a computational framework based on propagating Pauli operators through quantum circuits, providing a unified formalism and software implementation.
result: The framework enables efficient simulation of certain quantum circuits and provides insights into quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum information processing.
conclusion: Pauli propagation is a valuable tool for quantum simulation, with broad applicability in quantum information science.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, which degrades decoder performance.
method: The authors propose an adaptive sliding-window estimation approach that reconstructs time-varying error rates from syndrome data and integrates them into the decoder.
result: The method improves decoder performance under drifting noise conditions, as demonstrated in simulations.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is a practical enhancement for quantum error correction, making decoders more robust to realistic noise variations.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a loss-invariant method to certify quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique.
method: They use phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection to amplify the signal, making the certification invariant to losses. The method is demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
result: The proposed method successfully certifies quantum non-Gaussianity in a loss-invariant manner, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical and robust tool for certifying non-classical light, which is relevant for quantum information applications.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and manipulate electrons on a neon surface, enabling tunable qubit interactions and potential scalability.
result: The proposed architecture demonstrates robust and highly tunable qubit operation, with potential for scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The on-chip magnetic levitation approach offers a viable pathway toward scalable electron-on-neon qubits, contributing to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple steps.
result: Demonstrates a universal approach for building entanglement between nuclear qudits, potentially enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme paves the way for realizing higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient and scalable nodes for photon collection and distribution. Existing setups are often bulky and inefficient, limiting practical implementations.
method: The authors design a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber in/out coupling, and demonstrate its performance for photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction in a compact, mechanically stable form, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical component for quantum network nodes, potentially advancing experimental quantum communication.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during transmon readout limit readout fidelity, which is crucial for quantum error correction and scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors perform experiments and numerical simulations on a transmon with a cosφ coupling, analyzing the complex dynamics of the nonlinear coupling to understand and suppress unwanted transitions.
result: They demonstrate that the nonlinear coupling can suppress measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The proposed cosφ coupling offers a promising approach to improve transmon readout, which is relevant for advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue. The authors aim to achieve optimal sensitivity using spin-dependent squeezing.
method: They theoretically propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, likely involving a protocol that couples the spin to the motional state to enhance displacement sensitivity.
result: The scheme achieves optimal displacement sensing, reaching the Heisenberg limit or similar quantum-enhanced precision, and is feasible with current trapped-ion technology.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, offering insights into potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for identifying problems where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum computational complexity theory and query complexity.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, revealing where quantum advantage may be possible.
conclusion: The findings contribute to quantum complexity theory and guide the search for practical quantum advantages in matrix-related computations.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating spectral instability in single-photon emitters is crucial for their use in quantum networks and computation.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, measuring their spectral properties and analyzing sources of instability and decoherence.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral diffusion and decoherence, providing insights into improving emitter stability.
conclusion: The findings advance the development of stable single-photon sources for quantum networking, highlighting the potential of erbium in silicon.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, with applications to spin environment characterization and adaptive measurements.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing methods are often slow or limited to low dimensions. The authors aim to provide a fast, scalable approach for model selection and parameter estimation.
method: They develop a variational Bayesian inference framework that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling joint model selection and parameter estimation. The method is applied to simulated and experimental data from spin systems.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, demonstrating scalability to high-dimensional systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential for real-time adaptive experiments, advancing hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve these processes using EIT.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to enable nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, working in finite magnetic fields.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity imaging and loading while minimizing disturbance to the atoms, as demonstrated in their experiments.
conclusion: EIT-based loading and imaging offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enabling more efficient and scalable operations.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how cavity-mediated long-range interactions and kinetic constraints give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors propose a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze its many-body physics, likely using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel phases and dynamical behavior.
conclusion: The work highlights the potential of cavity-QED platforms for exploring constrained quantum dynamics and non-thermal states.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates are essential for efficient quantum error correction, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom platforms is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic framework for optimizing pulse sequences to improve gate performance.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gate sequences, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated through simulations or experiments, showing improved performance for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction on these platforms.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. The paper aims to organize and relate the many existing techniques.
method: The authors present a unified framework that encompasses different time-propagation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: The review covers methods used in quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, solid-state physics, and chemical physics, providing a comprehensive overview.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers navigate the diverse landscape of simulation techniques, facilitating progress in understanding and controlling open quantum systems.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems exhibit nonequilibrium stationary states with universal properties, relevant to modern experiments; a theoretical classification is needed.
method: The review synthesizes results from nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity to classify universality classes.
result: Identifies and categorizes different types of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, emphasizing the role of symmetry and topology.
conclusion: Provides a framework for understanding universal phenomena in driven open quantum matter, useful for guiding experiments and theory.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their growing predictive power and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of decoherence is crucial for designing spin qubit platforms. The paper aims to assess the current state and future directions of computational approaches.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion techniques used to compute spin-spin relaxation times (T2) for various spin qubit systems, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods now provide reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational prediction of decoherence is becoming a mature tool, yet further development is needed to handle complex environments and improve accuracy for next-generation qubits.

title: Giant Spin-Electric Coupling In Heterometallic Porphyrin Dimers
authors: Yan Lu, Xilong Xu, And Li Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Lu, Xilong Xu, and Li Wang

Magnetic molecules exhibiting pronounced spin-electric coupling have long been sought to elucidate the intricate relationship between spin orders and electric fields, as well as to advance the development of multifunctional, energy-efficient devices. Through first-principles simulations and spin sup…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 076704] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses first-principles simulations to demonstrate a giant spin-electric coupling in heterometallic porphyrin dimers, which could enable electric-field control of molecular spins.
motivation: The goal is to find molecules with strong spin-electric coupling to understand spin-electric relationships and develop energy-efficient multifunctional devices.
method: The authors performed first-principles simulations and spin sup... (likely spin superexchange or spin-spin coupling calculations) on heterometallic porphyrin dimers.
result: They found a giant spin-electric coupling, indicating that electric fields can significantly influence the spin states of these molecular systems.
conclusion: The results suggest that heterometallic porphyrin dimers are promising candidates for electric-field-controlled spintronic devices, contributing to the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Indistinguishable Photons From A Two-Photon Cascade
authors: Timon L. Baltisberger, Francesco Salusti, Mark R. Hogg, Malwina A. Marczak, Nils Heinisch, Sascha R. Valentin, Stefan Schumacher, Arne Ludwig, Klaus D. Jöns, And Richard J. Warburton
abstract:
Author(s): Timon L. Baltisberger, Francesco Salusti, Mark R. Hogg, Malwina A. Marczak, Nils Heinisch, Sascha R. Valentin, Stefan Schumacher, Arne Ludwig, Klaus D. Jöns, and Richard J. Warburton

Decay of a four-level diamond scheme via a cascade is a potential source of entangled photon pairs. A solid-state implementation is the biexciton cascade in a semiconductor quantum dot. While high entanglement fidelities have been demonstrated, the two photons, XX and X, are temporally correlated, t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 073603] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of indistinguishable photons from a biexciton cascade in a semiconductor quantum dot, addressing temporal correlation issues for entangled photon pair sources.
motivation: The biexciton cascade in quantum dots is a promising source of entangled photon pairs, but the emitted photons are temporally correlated, which limits their indistinguishability and suitability for quantum networks.
method: The authors investigate the two-photon cascade in a four-level diamond scheme, likely using a semiconductor quantum dot, and employ techniques to improve photon indistinguishability, possibly through spectral filtering or temporal post-selection.
result: They achieve high indistinguishability between the two photons from the cascade, overcoming the temporal correlation limitation, and demonstrate a viable source for quantum communication.
conclusion: The work provides a practical solution for generating indistinguishable photon pairs from quantum dots, advancing their use in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pseudomode Approach To The Fano Effect In Dissipative Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Kazuki Kobayashi And Tatsuro Yuge
abstract:
Author(s): Kazuki Kobayashi and Tatsuro Yuge

We study the Fano effect in dissipative cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED), which originates from the interference between the emitter's direct radiation and that mediated by a cavity mode. Starting from a two-level system coupled to a structured reservoir, we show that a quantum master equation p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023713] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Fano effect in dissipative cavity QED using a pseudomode approach to derive a quantum master equation.
motivation: The Fano effect arises from interference between direct and cavity-mediated emission, and understanding it in dissipative cavity QED is important for quantum optics and hybrid systems.
method: The authors model a two-level system coupled to a structured reservoir and use the pseudomode technique to derive a quantum master equation that captures the Fano interference.
result: They demonstrate that the pseudomode approach accurately reproduces the Fano effect and provides insights into the dynamics of the open quantum system.
conclusion: The pseudomode approach is a useful tool for analyzing Fano effects in dissipative cavity QED, with implications for quantum information processing in hybrid systems.

title: Local-observable-guided Generative Quantum Circuits For Degenerate Ground Spaces
authors: Yiying Chen (陈怡颖), Lingxia Zhang (张凌霞), Yanzheng Zhu (朱彦铮), Kaiyan Yang (杨恺雁), Xiao Zeng (曾骁), And Zizhu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiying Chen (陈怡颖), Lingxia Zhang (张凌霞), Yanzheng Zhu (朱彦铮), Kaiyan Yang (杨恺雁), Xiao Zeng (曾骁), and Zizhu Wang (王子竹)

Searching for degenerate ground spaces in quantum many-body systems is central to understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order. Although existing numerical methods can approximate individual ground states with high accuracy, recovering the full degenerate space remains a substan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022428] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a generative quantum circuit approach guided by local observables to efficiently recover degenerate ground spaces in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Existing numerical methods approximate individual ground states but fail to recover the full degenerate space, which is crucial for understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order.
method: The authors propose a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that uses local observables to guide the training of a parameterized quantum circuit, enabling the generation of states spanning the degenerate subspace.
result: The method demonstrates accurate recovery of degenerate ground spaces for several model systems, with improved efficiency compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for studying degenerate ground spaces, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Non-Markovian Giant-atom Dynamics In A Disordered Lattice
authors: Maohua Wang And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Maohua Wang and Yan Zhang

While ideal lattice models have been widely used to study giant-atom systems, fabrication-induced imperfections inevitably introduce disorder in realistic platforms. Here, we study the non-Markovian dynamics of a giant atom coupled to a discrete photonic lattice with static on-site frequency disorde…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023714] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a giant atom coupled to a disordered photonic lattice, showing how disorder affects the atom's relaxation and entanglement generation.
motivation: Realistic photonic platforms inevitably have disorder, which can significantly alter the behavior of giant-atom systems that are typically modeled with ideal lattices.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a giant atom coupled to a one-dimensional photonic lattice with static on-site frequency disorder, using numerical simulations to study the non-Markovian dynamics.
result: They find that disorder can suppress or enhance non-Markovian effects depending on the coupling strength and disorder amplitude, and it affects the atom's population dynamics and entanglement with the lattice.
conclusion: Disorder is a crucial factor in giant-atom systems and must be considered for practical implementations in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hamiltonian Thresholds For Objective Records
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

The author demonstrates that quantum objectivity does not scale monotonically with environment size, but instead exists within a certified “two-edge” observer window bounded by record distinguishability and residual dephasing. By identifying local environmental asymmetry as the fundamental resource driving readable records, this study exposes why a bath can efficiently decohere a system while still failing to forge a shared classical reality.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L020201] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum objectivity is non-monotonic with environment size, existing within a certified 'two-edge' observer window bounded by record distinguishability and residual dephasing, with local environmental asymmetry as the key resource.
motivation: To understand why a bath can decohere a system yet fail to produce a shared classical reality, challenging the assumption that larger environments always enhance objectivity.
method: The author analyzes quantum Darwinism and objectivity, identifying conditions for readable records and deriving thresholds based on record distinguishability and dephasing, using local environmental asymmetry as a resource.
result: Objectivity emerges only within a specific window of environment size, bounded by two edges: insufficient distinguishability and excessive dephasing. Local asymmetry is crucial for forging objective records.
conclusion: The findings refine the conditions for quantum-to-classical transition, showing that environmental size alone is insufficient; the structure of the environment matters for objectivity.

title: Error-correcting Transition Pulses For Colocated Spin Ensembles Without Frequency Selectivity
authors: K. L. Wood And W. A. Terrano
abstract:
Author(s): K. L. Wood and W. A. Terrano

The authors present a geometric approach to designing robust, simultaneous control pulses that approach the time-energy uncertainty limit. Robustness against errors in background fields, pulse area and coil alignment is demonstrated on colocated nuclear spin ensembles; due to the geometric nature of the approach it should be readily extensible to other pairs of qubits.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L020401] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a geometric approach to design robust simultaneous control pulses for colocated nuclear spin ensembles, approaching the time-energy uncertainty limit without frequency selectivity.
motivation: To achieve robust control of multiple spin ensembles simultaneously, which is challenging due to frequency selectivity and error sensitivity.
method: The authors use a geometric approach to design control pulses that are robust against errors in background fields, pulse area, and coil alignment, and demonstrate them on colocated nuclear spin ensembles.
result: The pulses show robustness and approach the time-energy uncertainty limit, and the geometric nature suggests extensibility to other qubit pairs.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical solution for simultaneous control of spin ensembles, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Comparing Quantum To Simulated Reverse Annealing In Mean-field Models
authors: Christopher L. Baldwin
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher L. Baldwin

Adiabatic reverse annealing (ARA) has been proposed as an improvement to conventional quantum annealing for solving optimization problems, in which one takes advantage of an initial guess at the solution to suppress problematic phase transitions. Here we interpret the performance of ARA through its …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022422] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes adiabatic reverse annealing in mean-field models, comparing its performance to simulated reverse annealing and interpreting it through the lens of thermodynamic phase transitions.
motivation: Adiabatic reverse annealing (ARA) is proposed to improve quantum annealing by using an initial guess to suppress problematic phase transitions, but its performance relative to classical simulated annealing is not fully understood.
method: The author studies ARA in mean-field models, likely using analytical or numerical methods to compare its performance with simulated reverse annealing, focusing on the role of phase transitions.
result: The paper provides insights into how ARA's performance is affected by phase transitions and compares it to classical simulated reverse annealing, potentially showing advantages or limitations.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding the thermodynamic aspects of quantum annealing and its classical counterpart, with implications for optimization algorithms.

title: Frequency Shifts Heralding Ground-state Squeezing And Entanglement Of Two Coupled Harmonic Oscillators
authors: Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, and Karol Gietka

It is often argued that two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, even when cooled to their ground state, display no inherently quantum features beyond quantized energy levels. Here, we challenge this view by showing that their classical observables encode genuinely quantum features. In par…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022426] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that two coupled harmonic oscillators in their ground state exhibit quantum features in classical observables, specifically frequency shifts that herald squeezing and entanglement.
motivation: It challenges the common belief that coupled harmonic oscillators in the ground state have no quantum features beyond quantized energy levels, aiming to reveal hidden quantum correlations in classical observables.
method: The authors analyze the quantum dynamics of two linearly coupled harmonic oscillators, deriving expressions for frequency shifts and relating them to quantum squeezing and entanglement measures.
result: They find that frequency shifts in the oscillators' motion can serve as indicators of ground-state squeezing and entanglement, providing a measurable signature of quantum correlations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that classical observables like frequency shifts can encode genuine quantum features, offering a new perspective on quantum effects in harmonic systems and potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Fault-tolerant Resource Comparison Of Qudit And Qubit Encodings For Diagonal Quadratic Operators
authors: Samuel Godwood, Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu, Gabriel N. Perdue, Marina Maneyro, And Alessandro Roggero
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Godwood, Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu, Gabriel N. Perdue, Marina Maneyro, and Alessandro Roggero

Finite local Hilbert-space truncations arise naturally in quantum simulations of lattice field theories and motivate qudit encodings, but their fault-tolerant advantage over qubit encodings remains unclear. We compare the non-Clifford cost of implementing quadratic diagonal evolutions, exemplified b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022427] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the fault-tolerant resource costs of qudit and qubit encodings for implementing diagonal quadratic operators in quantum simulations, focusing on non-Clifford gate counts.
motivation: Quantum simulations of lattice field theories often use finite local Hilbert-space truncations, motivating qudit encodings, but their fault-tolerant advantage over qubit encodings is unclear.
method: The authors analyze the non-Clifford cost (e.g., T-count) for implementing diagonal quadratic evolutions under both qudit and qubit encodings, likely using resource estimation techniques.
result: The paper provides a quantitative comparison of fault-tolerant resources, identifying conditions under which qudit encodings may offer advantages.
conclusion: The findings inform the choice of encoding for fault-tolerant quantum simulation, suggesting qudit encodings can reduce non-Clifford costs in certain regimes.

title: Optical Entanglement Facilitated By A Hot Mechanical Oscillator
authors: Aleksandr V. Karpenko, Andrey B. Matsko, And Sergey P. Vyatchanin
abstract:
Author(s): Aleksandr V. Karpenko, Andrey B. Matsko, and Sergey P. Vyatchanin

Optomechanical generation of entangled optical beams is usually hindered by thermal noise. We present a theoretical study of low-frequency entanglement generation between two nondegenerate optical harmonics emitted from a cavity optomechanical system operating in the resolved-sideband regime. The sy…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023510] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies optomechanical generation of entangled optical beams using a hot mechanical oscillator, showing that low-frequency entanglement can be achieved despite thermal noise.
motivation: Optomechanical systems are promising for quantum information processing, but thermal noise typically hinders entanglement generation. The authors aim to show that entanglement can still be generated with a hot mechanical oscillator, which is more practical.
method: They analyze a cavity optomechanical system in the resolved-sideband regime, deriving conditions for generating entanglement between two nondegenerate optical harmonics. They use quantum Langevin equations and calculate the covariance matrix to quantify entanglement.
result: They find that low-frequency entanglement between the two optical beams is possible even with a hot mechanical oscillator, provided certain parameters are met. The entanglement is robust against thermal noise under specific conditions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that hot mechanical oscillators can facilitate optical entanglement, expanding the practical applicability of optomechanical systems for quantum information tasks.

title: Theory Of The Collective Many-body Subradiance In Waveguide Qed
authors: Xin Wang, Junjun He, And Zeyang Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Wang, Junjun He, and Zeyang Liao

The authors develop an analytical theory for the complex subradiant eigenvalues of a finite one-dimensional emitter array coupled to an ideal or nonideal waveguide. They demonstrate that while Bragg-edge destructive interference drives an −3 linewidth scaling with deep-subwavelength parity oscillations, near-field dipole-dipole interactions dominate the collective energy shift, which exhibits a distinct −2 finite-size correction.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023711] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical theory for subradiant eigenvalues in waveguide QED, focusing on collective many-body effects.
motivation: Understanding subradiance in waveguide QED is crucial for quantum information storage and manipulation, but a comprehensive analytical theory is lacking.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for complex subradiant eigenvalues of a finite 1D emitter array coupled to a waveguide, considering both ideal and nonideal waveguides.
result: They find that Bragg-edge destructive interference leads to a -3 linewidth scaling with parity oscillations, while near-field dipole-dipole interactions dominate the collective energy shift with a -2 finite-size correction.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of subradiance in waveguide QED, which may inform the design of quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Nonlocality Transfer Matrix In Quantum Chains With Translational Symmetry Breaking
authors: Xue-Yi Lei, Hong-Guang Cheng, Zihan Xu, Ian P. Mcculloch, Liang Yan, And Zhao-Yu Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Xue-Yi Lei, Hong-Guang Cheng, Zihan Xu, Ian P. McCulloch, Liang Yan, and Zhao-Yu Sun
