authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new method to detect quantum dot charging energies by probing nuclear spin magnetism, relevant to spin qubit platforms.
motivation: Understanding charging energies in quantum dots is crucial for spin qubit operation, and existing methods may be limited. The authors propose a nuclear spin-based probe as an alternative.
method: They exploit the response of nuclear spins to electron charging in quantum dots, using nuclear magnetic resonance or similar techniques to infer charging energies.
result: The method successfully detects charging energies, providing a new tool for characterizing quantum dots.
conclusion: This approach offers a non-invasive way to probe quantum dot properties, potentially aiding in the development of spin qubit technologies.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to noise.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes gate parameters to achieve high-fidelity multiqubit entanglement gates, considering the ion-crystal dynamics.
result: The method enables scalable gate design for large ion crystals, demonstrating feasibility for hundreds of qubits with improved speed and robustness.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large-scale trapped-ion quantum computing by enabling efficient design of complex multiqubit gates.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that significantly improve the accuracy of Hamiltonian simulation with minimal overhead, reducing circuit depth for a given target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are simple but often require deep circuits. Improving their accuracy without large overhead is crucial for near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors propose injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas, which corrects leading error terms. They analyze the resulting error scaling and provide explicit constructions for various product formula orders.
result: The corrected product formulas achieve substantially lower circuit depth for a target accuracy compared to standard product formulas, with only a small increase in cost. They demonstrate improvements for both quantum and classical simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a practical and efficient way to enhance Hamiltonian simulation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices and also improving classical simulation methods.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction, providing polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is central to quantum many-body physics and quantum information, but exact contraction is often intractable. Approximate methods like belief propagation lack rigorous error control.
method: The authors propose systematic corrections to belief propagation, termed cluster corrections, which refine the approximation by considering local clusters of tensors. They derive rigorous bounds on the approximation error and show that the corrections lead to exponential convergence.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial-time contraction with error bounds that improve exponentially with the cluster size, outperforming standard belief propagation in accuracy for benchmark problems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximate tensor network contraction, with potential applications in quantum state simulation and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for quantum computing and simulation, leveraging their small mass for enhanced tunneling and continuous-variable operations.
motivation: To explore the unique advantages of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, which may enable new capabilities in quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3, such as its light mass and long-range interactions, and propose experimental implementations for tweezer arrays, including tunable hopping and continuous-variable encoding.
result: They demonstrate that helium-3's small mass leads to faster tunneling and stronger interactions, potentially improving quantum simulation of materials and enabling continuous-variable quantum computing with neutral atoms.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays offer a promising platform for quantum science, with potential advantages over other atomic species for certain applications.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array in a cryogenic environment extends Rydberg lifetimes by reducing blackbody radiation, which mitigates a major error source in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by decoherence from blackbody radiation, which shortens Rydberg lifetimes and reduces gate fidelities. The authors aim to address this bottleneck by cryogenically shielding the atom array.
method: They construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic apparatus and measure Rydberg lifetimes at low temperatures, comparing them to room-temperature values. They also characterize the impact on two-qubit gate error rates.
result: Cryogenic operation significantly extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing the dominant relaxation errors and improving the potential fidelity of two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic shielding is a practical and effective approach to enhance Rydberg-based quantum computing, offering a path toward higher-fidelity neutral-atom processors.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas, a hybrid quantum system, by mapping out spectral winding numbers and nonreciprocal behavior.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian topology in a tunable dissipative many-body platform, which is of fundamental interest in quantum physics and may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body system, tuning interactions and dissipation to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, and measure winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocal behavior, demonstrating non-Hermitian topology in a cold atomic system.
conclusion: The work establishes cold Rydberg gases as a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian physics, which could be relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics by decomposing the dynamics into standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally hard, and existing methods lack flexibility and efficiency. The authors aim to provide a highly configurable and efficient simulation approach using photonic hardware.
method: They decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements, enabling a photonic simulator that can be reconfigured for different models.
result: The proposed simulator is shown to be highly configurable and efficient for executing simulation algorithms, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The work offers a practical photonic platform for simulating quantum field dynamics, potentially advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient method for classically simulating small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using data from quantum computers.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is generally hard, but for small subregions of expectation landscapes, efficient classical surrogates may be possible, potentially aiding in variational quantum algorithms.
method: The authors propose a classical surrogate model that leverages initial data from quantum computers to predict expectation values in a local patch of the landscape, likely using techniques from quantum machine learning or classical shadows.
result: They demonstrate that such classical simulation can be done efficiently for small patches, with rigorous bounds on the required resources.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for reducing quantum resource requirements in hybrid quantum-classical algorithms, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-based reductions to make optimal stabilizer decompositions of multiqubit unitaries tractable, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage, but optimal stabilizer decompositions are often computationally intractable for large systems.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetries of the target unitaries to reduce the search space for optimal stabilizer decompositions, making the computation feasible for larger qubit counts.
result: The symmetry-accelerated approach extends the tractable regime for optimal stabilizer decompositions, allowing classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions provide a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices and the study of quantum advantage.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central computational task, and quantum algorithms promise speedups. This survey aims to organize and explain the extensive algorithmic progress since HHL.
method: The paper reviews the HHL algorithm and subsequent post-HHL developments, covering various quantum algorithmic techniques for the quantum linear system problem (QLSP).
result: Provides a thorough explanation of the algorithms, their complexities, and applications, serving as a reference for researchers.
conclusion: The survey consolidates the state of the art in quantum linear system solvers, highlighting their potential and open challenges.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, linking brickwork quantum circuits to exact solvability.
motivation: Quantum many-body dynamics are notoriously difficult to compute; space-time duality offers a unified framework to simplify and solve such dynamics.
method: The review synthesizes recent advances in space-time duality, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their role in exactly solvable models.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of how space-time duality enables exact solutions and connects to quantum computation concepts.
conclusion: The review establishes space-time duality as a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Robust Symmetry Breaking In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Chao Yin And Andrew Lucas
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Yin and Andrew Lucas

Using the two-dimensional random-bond Ising model as a concrete example, certain gapless ground states under quantum perturbations are shown to have a universal structure exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking, generalizing the classical Peierls argument for stability against thermal fluctuations.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070405] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that gapless quantum magnets with random-bond disorder exhibit robust spontaneous symmetry breaking, generalizing the classical Peierls argument to quantum perturbations.
motivation: Understanding the stability of symmetry-broken phases in gapless quantum systems is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics, with implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use the two-dimensional random-bond Ising model as a concrete example and analyze the effect of quantum perturbations on gapless ground states, extending the Peierls argument to the quantum case.
result: They demonstrate that certain gapless ground states under quantum perturbations have a universal structure exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking, robust against perturbations.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for understanding symmetry breaking in gapless quantum magnets, which may have implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Absence Of Far-detuned Attractive Optical Traps For Alkali Rydberg Atoms
authors: Gabriel E. Patenotte, Youngshin Kim, Samuel Gebretsadkan, And Kang-Kuen Ni
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel E. Patenotte, Youngshin Kim, Samuel Gebretsadkan, and Kang-Kuen Ni

Neutral-atom quantum simulation is susceptible to entanglement between the atom's internal electronic state and its center-of-mass position. In many alkali Rydberg platforms, the ‘‘spin-motion coupling’’ is exacerbated by the free expansion required to avoid ponderomotive antitrapping from optical f…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023103] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that far-detuned attractive optical traps are ineffective for alkali Rydberg atoms due to ponderomotive antitrapping, and proposes alternative trapping strategies.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum simulation suffers from spin-motion coupling in Rydberg platforms, exacerbated by free expansion to avoid ponderomotive antitrapping. The authors investigate whether far-detuned attractive traps can mitigate this issue.
method: The authors analyze the ponderomotive potential for alkali Rydberg atoms in far-detuned optical traps, considering both theoretical models and experimental constraints, and compare with alternative trapping schemes.
result: They find that far-detuned attractive traps are not viable for alkali Rydberg atoms because the ponderomotive force is inherently repulsive, leading to antitrapping. They suggest alternative approaches such as using blue-detuned traps or other techniques.
conclusion: The paper provides a fundamental limitation for optical trapping of Rydberg atoms, guiding future experimental designs for quantum simulation platforms.

title: Floquet Engineering Of Quantum Transport Through Two Driven Impurities
authors: Vincenzo Bruno, Corinna Kollath, Roberta Citro, And Ameneh Sheikhan
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Bruno, Corinna Kollath, Roberta Citro, and Ameneh Sheikhan

Floquet engineering offers powerful tools to manipulate quantum states by periodically driving physical parameters. In this work, we investigate the quantum transport through two periodically driven impurities in a mesoscopic one-dimensional channel. By mapping the time-dependent Hamiltonian into an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023313] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum transport through two periodically driven impurities in a one-dimensional channel using Floquet engineering.
motivation: To understand how periodic driving can manipulate quantum transport in mesoscopic systems, potentially enabling control of quantum devices.
method: The authors map the time-dependent Hamiltonian into a Floquet picture and analyze transport properties, likely using scattering or Green's function methods.
result: The paper reveals how driving parameters affect transport, possibly showing resonant or interference effects.
conclusion: Floquet engineering can be used to control quantum transport through impurities, with potential applications in quantum devices.

title: Dissipative Kondo Physics In The Anderson Impurity Model With Two-body Losses
authors: Matthieu Vanhoecke, Naoto Tsuji, And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Vanhoecke, Naoto Tsuji, and Marco Schirò

We study a dissipative version of the Anderson Impurity model, where an interacting impurity is coupled to a fermionic reservoir and exposed to Markovian dissipation in the form of two-body losses. Using a self-consistent hybridization expansion based on the noncrossing approximation (NCA), we compu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115110] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative Anderson impurity model with two-body losses using noncrossing approximation, revealing Kondo physics under dissipation.
motivation: Understanding how dissipation affects strongly correlated quantum systems, particularly the Kondo effect, is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors employ a self-consistent hybridization expansion based on the noncrossing approximation (NCA) to compute spectral functions and other observables.
result: They find that two-body losses modify the Kondo resonance, leading to a crossover from Kondo to local moment behavior as dissipation increases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into dissipative quantum impurity systems, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems, though not directly aligned with the core interests.

title: Stability Of Many-body Critical Phases
authors: Xingbo Wei, Beibei Tian, Zhao Liu, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Beibei Tian, Zhao Liu, and Yunbo Zhang

We investigate a many-body extended Aubry-André-Harper model and find that the many-body critical phase becomes ergodic when the boundary condition is changed from open to periodic in finite systems. The resulting ergodic phase satisfies the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and loses memory of i…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094202] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of many-body critical phases in an extended Aubry-André-Harper model, finding that changing boundary conditions from open to periodic can induce ergodicity and thermalization.
motivation: To understand the robustness of many-body critical phases and how boundary conditions affect their stability, which is relevant to quantum thermalization and ergodicity.
method: Numerical investigation of an extended Aubry-André-Harper model, comparing open and periodic boundary conditions in finite systems, and analyzing eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) and memory loss.
result: The many-body critical phase becomes ergodic under periodic boundary conditions, satisfying ETH and losing memory of initial conditions.
conclusion: Boundary conditions can destabilize many-body critical phases, leading to thermalization, which has implications for understanding quantum criticality and thermalization.

title: Distinct Many-body Scars And Emergent Quantum Phases Driven By Competing Interactions In Two-species Rydberg Arrays
authors: Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Shun-Yao Yu, Shi-Rong Peng, Jie Sheng, Su Yi, Peng Xu, Shou-Shu Gong, Tao Shi, And Jian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Shun-Yao Yu, Shi-Rong Peng, Jie Sheng, Su Yi, Peng Xu, Shou-Shu Gong, Tao Shi, and Jian Cui

Rydberg atom arrays composed of multiple atomic species stand as a highly promising platform for quantum computation. However, the underlying physics of these systems as quantum many-body systems remains poorly understood, owing to the intricate competition between attractive and repulsive interacti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115406] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies many-body scars and emergent quantum phases in two-species Rydberg arrays driven by competing interactions, focusing on non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the many-body physics of multi-species Rydberg arrays is crucial for their use in quantum computation, but the interplay of attractive and repulsive interactions leads to complex phenomena.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-species Rydberg array model with competing interactions, likely using numerical methods such as exact diagonalization or tensor networks to study the spectrum and dynamics.
result: They identify distinct many-body scar states and emergent quantum phases arising from the competition between interactions, revealing non-thermal behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in Rydberg arrays, which may inform quantum simulation and computation applications.

title: Transport And Localization In Driven Disordered Potentials With Quantum And Thermal Fluctuations
authors: Abdelâali Boudjemâa And Zohra Mehri
abstract:
Author(s): Abdelâali Boudjemâa and Zohra Mehri

The transport and localization of quantum droplets in time-dependent periodic disorder potentials are systematically studied. Our numerical results indicate that such exquisite periodically driven structures may support quantum phases that are principally different compared to static systems. We obs…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033158] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transport and localization of quantum droplets in driven disordered potentials, focusing on the interplay of quantum and thermal fluctuations.
motivation: Understanding how periodic driving and disorder affect quantum phases is important for controlling quantum systems, but the connection to information thermodynamics is indirect.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of quantum droplets in time-dependent periodic disorder potentials, analyzing transport and localization properties.
result: They observe quantum phases that differ from static systems, indicating that driven disorder can lead to novel localization and transport behavior.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of driven disordered systems, but its relevance to information thermodynamics is limited, as it does not directly address thermodynamic constraints or information processing.

title: Purcell-enhanced Electroluminescence Of A Unipolar Light-emitting Quantum Device At $λ=10\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}µ\mathrm{m}$
authors: Marta Mastrangelo, Djamal Gacemi, Axel Evirgen, Salvatore Pes, Alexandre Larrue, Pascal Filloux, Isabelle Sagnes, Abdelmounaim Harouri, Angela Vasanelli, And Carlo Sirtori
abstract:
Author(s): Marta Mastrangelo, Djamal Gacemi, Axel Evirgen, Salvatore Pes, Alexandre Larrue, Pascal Filloux, Isabelle Sagnes, Abdelmounaim Harouri, Angela Vasanelli, and Carlo Sirtori

Efficient generation of radiation in the mid- and far-infrared relies primarily on lasers and coherent nonlinear optical phenomena driven by lasers. This wavelength range lacks practical and efficient luminescent devices, particularly, because the spontaneous emission rate becomes much longer than t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033162] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Purcell-enhanced electroluminescence in a unipolar light-emitting quantum device at 10 µm, improving emission efficiency in the mid-infrared.
motivation: Efficient mid-infrared luminescent devices are lacking because spontaneous emission rates are slow; the authors aim to enhance emission via Purcell effect.
method: They fabricate a unipolar quantum device (likely quantum cascade-like) integrated with a microcavity to exploit the Purcell effect, and measure electroluminescence.
result: They observe Purcell-enhanced electroluminescence at λ=10 µm, indicating increased spontaneous emission rate and efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides a path toward efficient mid-infrared light sources, potentially useful for sensing and spectroscopy.

title: Dark-state Phase Transition To A Dark Soliton In A Dissipative Bose-Hubbard Chain
authors: Robbe Ceulemans, Samuel E. Begg, Matthew J. Davis, And Michiel Wouters
abstract:
Author(s): Robbe Ceulemans, Samuel E. Begg, Matthew J. Davis, and Michiel Wouters

We show that a Bose-Hubbard model with local loss exhibits a first-order dark-state phase transition between a dark soliton and a uniform superfluid. Semiclassical simulations and stability analysis reveal that the soliton acts as a many-body dark state, whose suppressed fluctuations modify the tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033146] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a first-order dark-state phase transition in a dissipative Bose-Hubbard chain, where a dark soliton emerges as a many-body dark state.
motivation: To understand the interplay between dissipation and interactions in many-body quantum systems, and to explore the role of dark states in non-equilibrium phase transitions.
method: The authors use semiclassical simulations and stability analysis to study the Bose-Hubbard model with local loss, identifying the dark soliton as a many-body dark state.
result: They find a first-order phase transition between a dark soliton and a uniform superfluid, with the soliton exhibiting suppressed fluctuations that modify the transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into dissipative quantum many-body physics and the emergence of dark states, but it is more focused on condensed matter physics than on information thermodynamics.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima, improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based solvers for QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima, limiting their accuracy in solving combinatorial optimization problems. The authors aim to enhance their performance by incorporating Floquet amplitude modulations.
method: The analog Floquet solver integrates Floquet amplitude modulations into the parametric oscillator network, allowing the system to dynamically escape local minima during the optimization process.
result: The Floquet-based approach significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator-based Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet engineering offers a promising technique to enhance the performance of Ising machines, potentially advancing their applicability in optimization tasks.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: This review covers nonequilibrium dynamics in photoexcited Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and photoinduced metastable states.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium states in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel optical responses and quantum metastable phases.
method: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways and mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution.

abstract:

Coulomb crystals form when the Coulomb interaction between charged particles dominates over kinetic energy; the prototype is the Wigner crystal formed by conduction electrons in metals at low densities. In recent years, it has become possible to realize Coulomb crystals using laser-cooled trapped ions, and these systems allow for unprecedented control of experimental parameters. This review describes the state of the art of ion Coulomb crystals in one, two, and three dimensions, their properties in and out of equilibrium, and their importance across fields ranging from condensed matter to astrophysics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 035001] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.

result: Summarizes the state of the art, highlighting unique control and tunability of ion Coulomb crystals and their importance for condensed matter and astrophysics.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals serve as versatile quantum simulators and model systems, but the paper's focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review covers tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution, a technique in nanoscale optical imaging.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize recent advances in tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy, which combines scanning probe techniques with optical fluorescence to achieve superresolution beyond the diffraction limit.
method: It reviews the principles and experimental implementations of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy, focusing on the use of a scanning tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine electromagnetic fields.
result: The technique enables atomic-scale spatial resolution in fluorescence imaging, revealing electronic and vibronic properties of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for studying molecular structures and reactions at the atomic scale, with potential applications in materials science and chemistry.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications

abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials, covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials has opened new avenues for studying magnetism in reduced dimensions, challenging existing theories and revealing novel phenomena.
method: The paper is a comprehensive review summarizing the current state of knowledge, including experimental and theoretical progress in 2D magnets, their interactions with light, phonons, and electric fields, and potential applications.
result: The review highlights the breadth of the field, encompassing ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field of 2D van der Waals magnets is rapidly evolving, expanding both fundamental understanding and application prospects.

Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars with future detectors and emphasizes multimessenger observations.
motivation: The paper aims to highlight the scientific potential of continuous gravitational wave searches and their connection to multimessenger astronomy.
method: It is a review article that surveys detection prospects, detector capabilities, and the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: The paper discusses the expected sensitivity of future detectors and the astrophysical implications of detecting continuous waves.
conclusion: Continuous gravitational wave astronomy offers a unique window into dense matter physics and requires coordinated multimessenger efforts.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from lattice geometry and correlations.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unconventional phenomena in kagome metals, which are driven by frustration and interference effects.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, discussing topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, superconductivity, and other phenomena.
result: It highlights the rich physics of kagome metals, including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematic states.
conclusion: Kagome metals serve as a platform for exploring strongly correlated topological physics, but the review does not directly contribute to the user's research directions.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for chemical, ecological, and epidemiological modeling.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for analyzing complex systems modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, which are prevalent in biology, sociology, and traffic flow.
method: The review presents field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and quantum field theory methods, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: It demonstrates how diverse approaches can be unified under a single framework, with applications to chemical systems, ecology, and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying tool for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes how gravitational-wave and X-ray observations of neutron stars constrain the dense matter equation of state, comparing to nuclear theory predictions.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial information about the behavior of matter under extreme compression, which is not directly accessible in terrestrial experiments.
method: The paper reviews recent observational results from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, and compares them to theoretical predictions from nuclear equation of state calculations extrapolated to high densities.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and the comparison with theory provides insights into the equation of state at supranuclear densities.
conclusion: The review highlights the current state of knowledge and outlines future observational opportunities to further constrain the dense matter equation of state.

authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes

In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research, highlighting progress and future opportunities.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental, theoretical, and simulation results in spin-glass dynamics.
result: The review tracks the evolution of the field and emphasizes the importance of combining experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass research benefits from interdisciplinary synergy, and future work should continue this approach.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but their realization in materials is challenging.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev model) and experimental progress in candidate materials, highlighting topological properties like chiral edge modes.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of Kitaev spin liquids and identifies promising materials.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview for researchers, but does not present new results directly relevant to the user's interests.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review connects statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to large-scale neural recordings, aiming to uncover reproducible collective behaviors in brain networks.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge theoretical statistical physics with quantitative neuroscience data to find predictive principles for brain function.
method: The paper reviews recent experimental and theoretical work, focusing on maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to multi-neuron recordings.
result: The review highlights that these methods reveal reproducible collective behaviors and provide predictive power comparable to other physics fields.
conclusion: Statistical physics offers a powerful framework for understanding neural network dynamics, but the work is primarily a review without novel technical contributions.

result: It summarizes the state of the art in modeling internal conversion and discusses potential applications.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.

tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To provide an overview of quantum properties of magnetic skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics and quantum technologies.
method: A review article summarizing theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum effects.
result: The paper discusses quantum aspects of skyrmions, such as quantum fluctuations and potential for quantum information processing, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit quantum properties that may be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker

result: It catalogs numerous experimental constraints and theoretical models for spin-dependent exotic interactions, highlighting the most sensitive searches and future prospects.
conclusion: The field is active and diverse, with many experimental approaches providing complementary constraints; future improvements in sensitivity may discover new physics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize the state of the art in theoretical nuclear astrophysics, addressing the challenge of measuring low-energy stellar reactions in the lab.
method: It reviews quantum-mechanical phenomena such as tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical approaches and proposed experimental techniques for studying stellar nuclear reactions.
conclusion: The paper is a valuable resource for nuclear astrophysics but does not align with the user's research interests in quantum information science.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that apparent violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivations.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how designing materials to violate these assumptions can lead to interesting properties.
method: The paper is a review (Colloquium) that surveys various circumstances where measurements exceed thermodynamic bounds and identifies which underlying assumptions are violated in each case.
result: It catalogs many examples of apparent violations and explains the assumptions behind each, also discussing how to engineer materials to exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but result from misapplying the bounds; understanding this can guide the development of novel materials.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses self-alignment in active matter systems, a topic in soft matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to unify and review the concept of self-alignment in active matter, which is a key mechanism in biological and robotic systems, but it is outside the user's research interests.
method: The paper provides a conceptual and mathematical framework for self-alignment, reviews existing models, and discusses applications.
result: It highlights how self-alignment leads to novel collective behaviors and offers a unified perspective on active systems.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a powerful principle in active matter with broad implications, but it is not relevant to the user's focus on quantum information and related fields.

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e− colliders, focusing on charmonium decays and searches for new charmoniumlike states.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize experimental progress in hadron spectroscopy, particularly charmonium decays, to validate QCD and understand quark confinement.
method: It is a colloquium review that surveys results from experiments like BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII, highlighting recent advances in measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
result: The review highlights BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements and summarizes recent findings on charmonium decays and new charmoniumlike states.
conclusion: The paper concludes that continued high-precision data from BESIII will further advance our understanding of strong interactions and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of the planetary radar system at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on its contributions to planetary science and near-Earth asteroid characterization.
motivation: The paper aims to document the achievements of the Arecibo radar system, which was the most sensitive of its kind, and to highlight its role in advancing planetary exploration.
method: The authors provide a historical overview, describing the radar techniques used and summarizing key observations of various Solar System bodies, including Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, and the Saturn system, as well as near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: The paper presents a comprehensive summary of the scientific output of the Arecibo radar, emphasizing its unique contributions to planetary surface and subsurface studies and its support for in situ missions.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system had a profound impact on planetary science, and its loss is significant; the paper serves as a record of its legacy.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo telescope's contributions to radio astronomy, not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory in radio astronomy, highlighting its scientific impact over five decades.
method: It provides a historical perspective, reviewing major upgrades and summarizing key discoveries in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
result: The paper presents a comprehensive overview of Arecibo's contributions, emphasizing its role in advancing radio astronomy.
conclusion: Arecibo's legacy is significant in astronomy, but the content is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.

result: The review highlights advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities enabled significant progress in geospace science, and the paper documents these contributions.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.

method: The authors review the physics of the precipitation bottleneck and describe how convection-cloud chambers reproduce key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation. They synthesize insights from experiments, theory, and computational models.

conclusion: Convection-cloud chambers offer a promising approach to understanding warm rain formation, but the topic is entirely outside the user's research interests in quantum information and related fields.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential violation of the cosmological principle, and its implications for the standard model of cosmology.
motivation: The cosmological principle is foundational to the standard model of cosmology, and testing its validity is crucial. The observed discrepancy between the cosmic microwave background dipole and the matter distribution dipole could challenge the standard model.
method: The authors review recent analyses of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, comparing the dipole in the matter distribution with the CMB dipole, and discuss potential biases and systematic effects.
result: The analyses reveal a significant inconsistency between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a need to revise the standard cosmological model, but further investigation is required to rule out systematic errors.

abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
